Everything below is verified. This decision authorizes one 136-attempt live
generation against the C5 tuned deployment. Single use, no reruns for wrong
answers.

  provider env contract               resolves, auth mode profile,

                                      base_url https://sjarmak.omniapp.co
  credential handling                 omni-cli profile store, 0600 in a 0700
                                      directory, no token in the process env,
                                      no .env, nothing tracked

EXACT BINDING

  condition             C4
  deployment_sha256     623d2214957a6fedcd0f92334fe856e1d504bf797a4ffdf3c37a1a23cd773187
  execution_plan_sha256 86bec4918d0f717950e09aa06ce5b891f81e768594cda66f81c201ebea1d1ca1

WHY THIS IS NOT AGENT-AUTONOMOUS

validate_c4_production_approval authenticates the receipt against a decision
bead that is closed with reason Responded, labeled human, and carries exactly
one comment of the form Response: followed by the canonical receipt JSON, closed
within 60 seconds of approved_at. An agent producing that comment would be
forging the human attestation the control exists to record. The receipt is
therefore yours to issue, not mine.

TO AUTHORIZE

Respond to this decision with the canonical receipt. A helper that emits the
canonical JSON and the exact bd command from the binding above is the next thing
I will write if you want it rather than hand-assembly.

DECLINING is also a clean outcome. The generation has not started, no receipt
exists, and nothing is consumed.

comments.author: sjarmak
comments.text:
BINDING CORRECTED. The earlier binding in this decision is superseded.

The run must execute with HEAD equal to the deployment source commit
3a7e52b, because verify_system_commit re-checks HEAD on every attempt and
verify_deployment_gate requires the v6 records' source_commit to equal the
system commit. Main HEAD had advanced four commits past it. Those four commits
change no runtime path, so the code is byte-identical, but one of them is what
committed the v6 deployment evidence, so a plain checkout would have deleted the
files the gate reads.

Resolution: a detached worktree pinned at 3a7e52b, with the deployment evidence
copied in as untracked (experiments is not a runtime path). Main is untouched
and free to move.

  worktree   /home/ds/projects/omni-benchmark-c5run
  HEAD       3a7e52b549a233c93fff3397f7551500de96807d
  guard      pinned, runtime paths clean
  venv       synced in the worktree, so imports resolve to the pinned src
             rather than main's editable install

CORRECTED BINDING

  condition             C4
  deployment_sha256     623d2214957a6fedcd0f92334fe856e1d504bf797a4ffdf3c37a1a23cd773187
  execution_plan_sha256 3c79809a38d29d6cafaf00f7c5fd825540c2e3e693a2c6784dd83020b96bccfa
  output_root           /home/ds/projects/omni-benchmark-c5run/runs/c5-dev-a-generation-v1
  run_id                c5-dev-a-generation-v1
  schedule_sha256       40200e4555e69c2a6b1a5fc52d61dcf49de4a6a38e4c69461d3f37ab3e47eeaa
  system_commit         3a7e52b549a233c93fff3397f7551500de96807d

Only execution_plan_sha256 and output_root changed. The schedule and deployment
digests are unchanged, which is the expected result of moving the workspace and
nothing else.

TO AUTHORIZE

scripts/make_approval_receipt.py assembles the canonical receipt and writes the
exact response body, so nothing is hand-typed into a 60-second window:

  uv run python scripts/make_approval_receipt.py
    --workspace /home/ds/projects/omni-benchmark-c5run
    --system-commit 3a7e52b549a233c93fff3397f7551500de96807d
    --freeze-a-commit 7d39ee107338da1ce10e2553a4290e64bfc2f892
    --run-id c5-dev-a-generation-v1
    --output-root /home/ds/projects/omni-benchmark-c5run/runs/c5-dev-a-generation-v1
    --deployment-root /home/ds/projects/omni-benchmark-c5run/experiments/deployments/c5-dev-a-v6
    --deployment-run-id c5-dev-a-deployment-v6
    --decision-bead-id omni-benchmark-czf
    --receipt-path /home/ds/projects/omni-benchmark-c5run/receipt.json

It prints the two-command sequence that comments the canonical response and
closes this decision as Responded. Run those yourself; the comment is the
attestation, and an agent writing it would make the record false.

title: Thread the generation freeze separately from the control freeze in sealed scoring
description:
Cohort run manifests hard-record the generation freeze sha256 (Freeze B v7, e1c9f196...ae4730). load_sealed_output_batch and _load_cohort in sealed_evaluation.py currently receive whichever freeze the caller passes them, with no distinction between the freeze that produced the artifacts and the freeze that governs the current scoring code. Scoring under the corrected system's Freeze B v8 (386bfebd...) therefore rejects all 12 sealed cohorts at sealed_evaluation.py:716 with "sealed cohort run manifest is invalid," because SealedRunManifest.from_dict validates the v7-stamped manifest against v8.

The fix: artifact validation must bind to the generation freeze that actually produced the artifacts, while the control gate (_require_exact_control_checkout in sealed_evaluation_cli.py:171) continues to bind to the current scoring system's commit. These are two different concerns that a single freeze_b argument currently conflates.

Touch points: load_sealed_output_batch and _load_cohort in sealed_evaluation.py, plus their callers in sealed_evaluation_cli.py. Loading the v7 manifest currently requires load_freeze_b_control, which re-asserts HEAD == 94cc0d9 (the original control commit). A load path is needed that validates the generation-freeze binding without re-asserting the control gate, since the control gate must instead validate against the current (v8, or later) system commit.

Every existing integrity check must be preserved. This is about passing the right freeze to the right check, not relaxing either one. Tests ship in the same commit as the fix.

While in there, add a --test-ids flag to sealed_evaluation_cli.py and sealed_test_release.py. Both currently default to the original 101-question TEST_IDS_PATH (data/manifests/test_ids.txt), which Freeze B never froze; only sealed_dispatch_cli.py exposes the flag today, which is why generation used the correct 89-question sealed_mvp_ids.txt frame but scoring and gold release do not without a driver workaround.

Completing this work requires recording another Freeze B manifest (the recipe is in docs/handoff-2026-08-30-sealed-scoring.md, "Recipe: how the v8 re-freeze was done"), since the CLI change moves HEAD again.

Source of truth: docs/handoff-2026-08-30-sealed-scoring.md, sections "The blocker, precisely" and "The agreed fix, not yet started".
close_reason: Split-freeze implementation, successor control, and exact no-gold preflight complete

comments.author: sjarmak
comments.text:
2026-08-30 E02 join-path assessment. Full writeup in docs/e02-join-path-assessment.md. Analysis only; nothing deployed, no HEAD movement, no protocol or frozen artifact touched.

VERDICT. E02 declares real join paths on the topics the agent queries. compile_e02_relationship_bundle rewrites each compiled topic's empty joins map to a target-view map, flips validation.joins_generated to True, and writes a top-level relationships file. The deployment loader recognizes both surfaces (omni_semantic_deployment._deployment_file handles the relationships name; topics deploy by name with joins intact and are readback-verified). e02_publication_validation builds 18 deployment plans, 272 files, 91 relationship contracts, candidate set sha256 db811d6ec553d3b82e42ba3bbd9bafe7ca528a695836a33d6f1aff0b60c5b074. E02 is therefore a direct test of the mechanism in docs/c4-query-path-disclosure.md, not a correlational bet.

EMITTED. Baseline: 0 of 127 topics with joins, joins_generated False everywhere. E02: 67 of 127 topics with joins, joins_generated True on 16 of 18 databases, 91 relationship contracts, semantic_elements byte-identical to baseline on all 18 databases (zero metric-disposition changes, exact). Only the relationship half of E02's registered spec does anything; no deferred metric was reclassified in any database.

FK funnel: 1228 public FKs, 1049 pass the conservative contract (281 exactly_one, 768 zero_or_one, 0 multi-column), 179 deferred all for target_not_unique. Only 91 of 1049 reach a bundle, because both endpoints must be published views and both FK columns must be published as one-to-one bound dimensions. Published surface is 6 to 11 views per database against 47 to 63 tables.

Two different sixteens: the inventory 16 is how many of the 18 compiled databases carry a relationship; the deployment 16 is the schedule-derived set. Same size, different membership.

DEPLOYED SLICE (the 16 databases the E02 CLI targets, which are the 16 the v8 C4 baseline ran against): 85 of 91 relationships, 14 of 16 databases gain at least one declared join, 61 of 114 topics gain at least one, 0 of 114 topics declare a measure. Topic out-degree: 53 zero, 39 one, 20 two, 2 three. Every join is many_to_one, always_left, reversible false, emitted only on the FK-holding topic, one level deep.

COVERAGE OF THE 62 MULTI-RELATION ATTEMPTS. Reproduced the published 62 exactly (2 correct, 41 wrong, 19 error). 173 distinct non-CTE source references; 142 resolve to a published view, 3 name a real unpublished table, 28 name nothing public.
- 16 of 62 (25.8%): every source view covered by one topic's declared one-hop join set. Outcomes 1 correct, 12 wrong, 3 error. 3 of the 31 class-A failures.
- 18 of 62 (29.0%): all sources modeled and connected through declared relationships, but not within one topic's one-hop set. Omni topic joins nest; E02 emits one level. A transitive-path compiler variant would roughly double coverage if Omni honors nesting.
- 7 of 62 (11.3%): all modeled, no declared relationship links them.
- 21 of 62 (33.9%): at least one source is not a published view. Out of reach for any model-declaration change.
16 of 62 is the ceiling on where a compiled path would have existed, not an estimate of where it would have been taken.

SUFFICIENCY. Necessary, not sufficient. Zero measures in both baseline and candidate, at both topic and view level, measured across all 114 deployed topics. 85 of 133 parseable governed attempts contain an aggregate, 46 of the 62 multi-relation ones, and 11 of the 16 E02 would give a join path. So for 11 of those 16 the agent still has a reason to rewrite. E02 alone leaves 5 of 62 fully composable from declared structure. Counter-evidence that E02 could still shift the path: PF-004 records Omni natively inferring many-to-one joins onto a topic whose fields list named only its base view, so the shape E02 emits is the product's own default shape.

A measures change is a second intervention, not an addition. It has no declared public source of truth comparable to a foreign key (the HKB half of E02 produced zero reclassifications), it puts row multiplication on top of many_to_one joins which is E02's own automatic-revert condition, and it needs compiler plus deployment-readback work.

ORDERING RECOMMENDATION.
1. Run E02 as built, unchanged. The run answers the one question no offline analysis can: does Omni's agent change path when a declared join exists. rewriteSql, join_via_map, and join_paths_from_topic_name are already captured per attempt and the existing analyzer reads them. Set accuracy expectations low in advance: at most 15 non-correct attempts sit in the declared-path bucket, 11 still need an undeclared aggregate, and 1 currently-correct attempt sits there and can regress. Do not relax the keep/revert gate to protect it; the path measurement is the value.
2a. If the path moves, spend the next slot on declared measures, with the row-multiplication audit the registration already specifies.
2b. If the path does not move, do not build measures. Spend the next slot on E03, which pays off through the rewrite path the agent demonstrably uses.
3. Nested-join E02 variant (addresses the 18 connected-but-multi-hop) sits below both; worthless until the path question is answered.
NOT E05. Precondition measured and failed: ceiling 6 of 31 against a target of 16, floor 0, and 24 of 31 select no compiled field at all. Already recorded INCONCLUSIVE. It should not consume an evaluation slot. The narrow reporting fix inside it (generated_sql recorded as null while the executed SQL sits in userEditedSQL) is worth fixing in the optimized arm and costs no slot.
NOT the published-view widening. Largest single gap by count (21 of 62) but a much larger change to the evaluated surface with no conservative public contract behind it. Not under deadline.

OPEN. Whether Omni composes through a declared join. Whether it honors nested topic join paths. Whether a base-view-only topic fields list exposes joined fields (PF-004 is evidence, not proof).

title: Restore silently dropped 71 tables across two databases via case-sensitive dump lookup
description:
The mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large mirrors are missing 34 and
37 tables respectively because restore resolves dump files case-sensitively
while the upstream dump ships lowercase filenames. The data is present locally
and fully recoverable. This is a provisioning defect in this repository, not an
upstream benchmark defect, not a broken Neon restore, and not a reader-grant
problem.

MEASUREMENT

Declared tables come from data/raw/livesqlbench-large-v1/schema/<db>/<db>_schema.txt,
restored counts from config/databases/livesqlbench-large-v1.json verification.table_count.

  mental_healths_large     55 declared, 21 restored, 34 missing
  organ_transplant_large   57 declared, 20 restored, 37 missing

All 16 other databases show zero missing tables.

The missing sets are exactly the scorer_omitted_tables entries recorded for
those two databases: 34 and 37. Case-insensitively, every declared table has a
dump file; 55 of 55 and 57 of 57 resolve. Case-sensitively, 0 of 34 and 0 of 37
of the omitted names resolve, and every one of them has a dump file that differs
only in capitalization.

  omitted 'Facilities'               actual dump file 'facilities.sql'
  omitted 'Patients'                 actual dump file 'patients.sql'
  omitted 'AssessmentBasics'         actual dump file 'assessmentbasics.sql'
  omitted 'Demographics'             actual dump file 'demographics.sql'
  omitted 'HLA_Info'                 actual dump file 'hla_info.sql'
  omitted 'Function_and_Recovery'    actual dump file 'function_and_recovery.sql'

MECHANISM

database_postgres.py restore_database builds each candidate as
dump_root / f"{table}.sql" from restore_order, and for any table listed in
omitted_tables it asserts the candidate does NOT exist, then skips it. Because
the omitted names are CamelCase and the shipped files are lowercase, that
non-existence assertion passes on a case-sensitive filesystem. The missing data
was therefore recorded as an intentional omission rather than raised as a
restore failure. scorer_continues_after_sql_error is also True for both
databases. Both fields were introduced in de7ed6d.

WHY EVERY DOWNSTREAM CHECK PASSED

verification.schema_sha256 and content_sha256 were computed after the truncated
restore, so they fingerprint the truncated state and match it exactly.
readonly_role_verified and external_parity are both True against that same
truncated state. This is why omni-benchmark-2j9 was closed as refuted: its live
parity check was correct about what it compared and could not have detected
this.

IMPACT

- 18 dev-A questions (9 per database) currently unscorable.
- 54 attempts in the completed direct baseline scored gold_statement_error;
  that category was correct, since the benchmark gold references tables that
  were never loaded.
- Both databases' share of the sealed 101, since the split is stratified by
  database. Freeze B must not commit these snapshot identifiers as they stand.
- omni-benchmark-wk0 was drafted assuming these 18 questions were permanently
  unrecoverable. That assumption is now wrong and its option set changes again.

FIX

1. Correct dump-file resolution so a capitalization-only mismatch is an error
   rather than a silent skip. An omitted-table declaration must not be
   satisfiable by a case variant of an existing file.
2. Clear scorer_omitted_tables for both databases and re-derive
   scorer_continues_after_sql_error.
3. Re-provision both Neon mirrors and regenerate their verification
   fingerprints. This is an external infrastructure action requiring per-action
   authorization.
4. Re-run the affected C1-C3 attempts. This is a demonstrable failure outside
   the evaluated system under the protocol's rerun policy, so it is a
   permitted rerun rather than an answer-dependent one; record the disposition
   before re-running.
5. Audit the other 16 databases for the same class of silent skip even though
   their table counts currently reconcile.
acceptance_criteria: Dump-file resolution rejects capitalization-only mismatches with an explicit error and a regression test covers it. scorer_omitted_tables is empty for mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large. Both mirrors re-provisioned under per-action authorization, verification.table_count equals 55 and 57, and fingerprints regenerated as new append-only records. Affected C1-C3 attempts re-run under a recorded pre-run disposition. All 18 databases audited for the same class of silent skip.
notes:
2026-08-29 code fix landed for steps 1 and 5; steps 2, 3 and 4 remain and need
human authorization. Working tree only, nothing committed.

WHAT CHANGED

New module src/omni_benchmark/dump_coverage.py resolves a restore order against
a dump directory independently of the database client, so the same resolution
can be audited offline. index_dump_files maps each casefolded dump stem to its
file and raises DumpCoverageError when two files differ only in capitalization.
describe_dump_coverage reports rather than raises, returning load paths in
restore order plus missing tables, case mismatches, and contradicted omissions.

restore_database in database_postgres.py now delegates resolution to that module
and raises on any contradicted omission, naming both the omitted table and the
dump file that contradicts it. Identifier validation still runs over restore
order and omissions before any filesystem or client work, so the path-traversal
and symlink guards are unchanged.

New CLI subcommand: omni_benchmark.database_cli verify-dump-coverage
--dump-root <root> --restore-order <path>. It reports every inventory database
without contacting PostgreSQL and exits 1 if any database is incomplete.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE ORIGINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERION

This bead was filed asking that resolution reject capitalization-only
mismatches. Implementing that would have left the restore broken, because the
mismatch is in the restore order rather than in the dump: facilities.sql
contains CREATE TABLE public.facilities, and the schema file declares the table
unquoted and lower case. The filename is only a selector; the file carries the
authoritative identifier. Resolution is therefore case-insensitive and
unambiguous, and the strictness moved to where the data loss actually happened:
an omission can no longer be satisfied by a case variant. Case-insensitive
collisions inside one directory are rejected outright.

AUDIT ACROSS ALL 18 DATABASES

Run against the real upstream dumps at
data/raw/livesqlbench-large-v1/extracted/postgre_table_dumps_large with
config/databases/restore-order-large-v1.json. Exit code 1.

  mental_healths_large     55 ordered, 21 resolvable, 34 contradicted omissions
  organ_transplant_large   57 ordered, 20 resolvable, 37 contradicted omissions
  other 16 databases       complete

Totals: 71 contradicted omissions, 0 genuinely missing dump files. The single
omission on labor_certification_applications_large is genuine; that table has no
dump file under any capitalization, so 50 ordered resolve to 49 and the database
reports complete. This confirms the defect is confined to the two databases and
that no other database is silently truncated.

TESTS

tests/test_dump_coverage.py, seven cases covering collision rejection,
case-insensitive resolution, contradicted omissions, genuine upstream
omissions, missing dumps, and order preservation. Three regression cases added
to tests/test_database_postgres.py and two to tests/test_database_cli.py, the
latter driven by the real committed inventory and restore order. Full suite:
1,512 passed, 3 expected environment skips. Ruff check and format clean.

REMAINING

Step 2, clearing scorer_omitted_tables and scorer_continues_after_sql_error for
the two databases, is deliberately not done here. That edit changes
config/databases/livesqlbench-large-v1.json, whose SHA-256 is pinned as
inventory_sha256 in config/conditions/direct-database-targets-v1.json and
verified against published run sidecars by direct_database_loader.py. It also
must land together with step 3, since clearing the omissions without
re-provisioning leaves verification.table_count inconsistent, and re-provisioning
without clearing them drops the same 71 tables again. Steps 3 and 4 are external
actions requiring per-action authorization.

Step 1 (code fix) committed as f5f756b on main: new dump_coverage module,
restore_database resolution rewritten, verify-dump-coverage subcommand.
7 files, 516 insertions, 18 deletions. Suite 1512 passed, branch coverage 84.23%.

Implementation diverges from this bead's original acceptance criterion, which asked
resolution to reject capitalization-only mismatches. That would have left the restore
broken: facilities.sql contains CREATE TABLE public.facilities and the schema declares
the table unquoted, so the file is correct and only the filename differs. Resolution is
case-insensitive; the strictness moved to omissions, which are now refused when any
capitalization of the file exists. Reasoning recorded in D-071.

Steps 2-4 remain, each needing per-action authorization:
 2. clear scorer_omitted_tables and scorer_continues_after_sql_error for
    mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large in
    config/databases/livesqlbench-large-v1.json, and correct verification.table_count
    (21 to 55, 20 to 57). That file's SHA-256 is pinned as inventory_sha256 in
    config/conditions/direct-database-targets-v1.json and verified against published
    run sidecars, so the pin has to move with it.
 3. re-provision both Neon mirrors from the full dump set.
 4. re-run the affected C1-C3 attempts under the rerun policy (infrastructure failure
    outside the evaluated system, not a wrong answer).
Steps 2 and 3 land together or the recorded table_count contradicts the deployed
database.


RETRACTED 2026-08-29. This bead's premise is false and its fix is reverted.

The pinned upstream loader init-databases_postgresql_large_v1.sh lines 118-127
resolves each dump as <table>.sql with an exact filename match and skips with a
warning on a miss. Its list spells the table Facilities; the archive ships only
facilities.sql; the pinned image is Linux. So the OFFICIAL reference database is
built without those 34 and 37 tables. This repository reproduced that on purpose,
which docs/database-setup.md already stated.

Arithmetic: mental_healths_large_template holds 57 dump files, 21 with capital
letters, and verification.table_count is 21. 55 declared minus 21 loaded is 34,
element for element the committed scorer_omitted_tables. organ_transplant_large
gives 20 of 57 with 37 omitted. The restore was never truncated relative to its
target.

Commit f5f756b would have loaded the lowercase files, building two databases
holding tables the scorer's does not, and breaking comparability with published
LiveSQLBench numbers. It also made the correct configuration unrestorable, since
it refused a declared omission whose case variant exists. Its behavior is reverted.

Kept in corrected form: dump_coverage and verify-dump-coverage, reframed from
completeness to fidelity. They now assert scorer_omitted_tables equals the set the
official loader actually skips. Against the real archive all 18 databases pass,
exit 0.

The real finding moves to the follow-up bead: 27 dev-A questions are unanswerable
in the official environment and need an exclusion record, not a repair.
Full reasoning in docs/research-log.md D-072; D-071 is marked retracted.
close_reason: Refuted: upstream loader behavior, faithfully reproduced. Fix reverted. See D-072.

title: Reconcile dev-A coverage rule with C4 deployment footprint before v5 dispatch
description:
The dev-A intervention preregistration committed at 82f0d4f cannot be satisfied
by the C4 arm that is currently prepared for launch. This is a frame decision on
a human-controlled surface (scoring definitions), not an agent task, and it must
be settled BEFORE the v5 dispatch, because settling it after any C4 number
exists converts it into a post-hoc frame change.

ARITHMETIC

experiments/planned-dev-a-interventions-v1.json states:
- common_evaluation.promotion_condition: C4 is the promotion condition for
  E01-E03.
- common_evaluation.full_dev_a_requirement: an intervention that cannot be
  evaluated on all 154 dev-A questions is INCONCLUSIVE and cannot be promoted.
- stopping_rule: stop early if full dev-A coverage cannot be achieved.

The prepared C4 baseline v5 resolves ten deployment targets, and its dev-A
scoring gate in docs/human-decisions.md is
--expected-official-scoreable-questions 85.

154 dev-A questions span 18 databases. C4 is deployed on 10. At most 85 of 154
dev-A questions are C4-scoreable. Therefore every intervention E01-E03 is
INCONCLUSIVE by construction and the stopping rule fires before E01 begins.

Direct-side coverage is separately incomplete. Of 154 dev-A questions, 32 are
unreachable today:
- mental_healths_large (9) and organ_transplant_large (9): benchmark gold SQL
  does not execute against the restored databases; see omni-benchmark-2j9.
- archeology_scan_large (5) and cybermarket_pattern_large (9): excluded by
  pre-run disposition in config/conditions/public-baseline-exclusions-v1.json,
  scope public-only-c1-c3-baseline.

Counts derived by joining data/manifests/dev_a_ids.txt against the public
selected_database field of data/manifests/eligible_questions.jsonl. No gold,
hidden annotation, or test-split content was read.

OPTIONS

A. Amend full_dev_a_requirement to the C4-deployed frame: all dev-A questions in
   the ten deployed databases, with the frame fixed and committed before the
   first intervention. Cheap, committable today, preserves preregistration
   integrity as long as it lands before any C4 result exists.

B. Hold the 154 rule and wait for omni-benchmark-dih.17 to deploy all 18
   databases. Stronger evaluation, but gated on dih.17.2 and dih.17.3, which are
   open compiler defects.

Independent of A or B: cybermarket_pattern_large can be recovered now. Its
external reader credential is already repaired and verified per the exclusion
record; the exclusion persists only because the original launch evidence
predates the fix. Re-running it into the direct baseline recovers 9 dev-A
questions.

NOTE ON THE SEALED RUN

The development-frame choice does not relieve dih.17. D-046 records the plan as
running C4 once all 18 isolated deployments pass validation and exact readback,
and the split was stratified by database, so the sealed test requires C4 on
every database regardless of what is decided here. Option A buys a development
signal earlier; it does not shorten the path to Freeze B.
acceptance_criteria: A committed decision selecting option A or option B, landed before any public-c4-baseline-v5 result exists. If A, experiments/planned-dev-a-interventions-v1.json records the deployed-frame coverage rule and the fixed database list. If B, omni-benchmark-aez.7.1 stays blocked until omni-benchmark-dih.17 reports 18 validated deployments. Either way the disposition of mental_healths_large, organ_transplant_large, archeology_scan_large, and cybermarket_pattern_large is recorded with the same evidence discipline as the existing exclusion config.
notes:
2026-08-29 correction to the option set. Option B as written is not reachable.
omni-benchmark-2j9 is CLOSED as refuted: both databases match committed
schema/content fingerprints and all 81 receipts bind the correct attested
read-only target. Separately, all 54 unscorable dev-A attempts carry
failure_category gold_statement_error, exactly mental_healths_large 27 plus
organ_transplant_large 27. So the benchmark gold does not execute there while
the restore is provably correct, and no amount of deployment work in
omni-benchmark-dih.17 recovers those 18 dev-A questions. Full 154-question
dev-A coverage is therefore unachievable by anyone, and the preregistered
full_dev_a_requirement must be reframed rather than waited out. The remaining
decision is only what the frame is.

Two hypotheses for the two databases were tested and refuted today. Missing
preprocess step: no question in any of the 18 databases has non-empty
preprocess_sql. Schema qualification or search_path: the committed schema files
for both databases create unqualified public-schema tables, and neither
postgres_execution.py nor direct_sql_capture.py sets search_path.

Leading untested hypothesis: the per-database read-only reader credential holds
catalog access but lacks SELECT on data tables. That fits every observation at
once, including the ones that refuted the earlier readings: catalog
introspection succeeds, every data-table reference fails regardless of
condition, benchmark gold fails, and a catalog-based schema fingerprint still
matches exactly because permissions are not part of it. Direct precedent exists
in this project: cybermarket_pattern_large was excluded after its database
privilege preflight failed, and its external reader credential was later
repaired and verified. Test is one read-only SELECT against one data table per
database using the attested reader. That is a diagnostic, not a rerun, and it
does not require any credential mutation. If it confirms, the disposition is a
grant repair and 18 dev-A questions plus their share of the sealed test are
recovered; if it refutes, the disposition is an exclusion record with the same
evidence discipline as public-baseline-exclusions-v1.json.

Note that SQLSTATE is currently discarded at direct_sql_capture.py, which is
why this could not be settled from existing telemetry. See omni-benchmark-bfb.
2026-08-29 second correction to the option set; supersedes the note above. The
18 dev-A questions on mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large are
recoverable. omni-benchmark-39b establishes that restore dropped 34 and 37
tables through case-sensitive dump-file resolution, the data ships in the
upstream dump as lowercase files, and the benchmark gold is not defective. The
reader-grant hypothesis recorded in the previous note is refuted; no live query
was needed to settle it. Once 39b is repaired, dev-A coverage returns to 145 of
154, short only by archeology_scan_large (5) unless its exclusion is revisited,
and by cybermarket_pattern_large (9) unless it is re-run. Decide wk0 after 39b
lands rather than against the current numbers.

title: Two database environments fail uniformly across all conditions; classification and restore both in question
description:
Found 2026-08-28 23:05Z while monitoring public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1
at 307 captures. Not acted on: the classification question is a human-controlled surface.

OBSERVATION

  organ_transplant_large    0 ok / 39 attempts   (c1 0/13, c2 0/13, c3 0/13)
  mental_healths_large      4 ok / 42 attempts   (c1 2/14, c2 1/14, c3 1/14)

Those two databases account for all 48 database_statement_error in the run. The other
eight databases seen so far have zero. The failure is total, flat across three different
scaffolds, and confined to two databases. That pattern is what a broken environment looks
like; it is not what a model-capability difference looks like, because a capability
difference would vary by condition and these do not.

Supporting detail from organ_transplant_large/c1/organ_transplant_3-r1: the attempt
degrades from a three-table join, to a simpler join, to SELECT * FROM transplant_matching
LIMIT 5, which is the shape of a client probing after repeated rejections.

NOT ESTABLISHED

No error text was recovered. attempt.trace.jsonl records metadata_sha256 rather than
message bodies, which is the telemetry contract working as designed, and the benchmark
databases are not in the local postgres instance, so no direct query was attempted. A
broken restore and a genuinely hostile schema are still both consistent with the evidence.
Someone with the database environment in hand can settle it in one query.

IMPACT ON EVERY CONDITION-LEVEL NUMBER REPORTED TODAY

                     all 10 DBs      excluding the two
  c1                  52.9%              68.8%
  c2                  71.3%              95.9%
  c3                  50.5%              67.1%
  c2 vs c3        z=3.04 p=0.0023    z=4.53 p<0.0001
  c1 vs c3             --             z=0.23 p=0.8190

D-066 survives and sharpens rather than dissolving: C2 answers 96% on the clean eight
while C1 and C3 are indistinguishable at about 68%. But every absolute rate in D-066 and
in the RUN-CLASSES census is depressed roughly 16 points by these two databases.

THE CLASSIFICATION QUESTION, FOR A HUMAN

These 81 attempts carry failure_origin=evaluated_system. If the environments are broken
the origin is infrastructure, and the protocol rerun policy covers exactly that case
("reruns require a demonstrable failure outside the evaluated system"). Scoring them as
the system failing 81 questions would understate every condition. Reclassification is a
custody and scoring surface; proposing, not changing.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING

The run id says 16db and ten distinct databases have appeared at 307 of 518 captures.
Either more are pending in the remaining attempts or the deployment covers fewer

Condition 3 is the one that catches this failure class and nothing in the current launch path checks it.

title: Preserve content-refusal versus insufficient-context outcomes

acceptance_criteria: TDD proves cannot_answer_safely maps to refused_content and insufficient_information maps to no_answer_insufficient_context through raw capture, batch reconciliation, failure aggregation, and scoring-compatible telemetry; answered/errored remain unchanged; action reason is captured without exposing secrets; D-051 fake-account and replay2 evidence are rechecked from preserved model actions/transcripts; focused/full tests, Ruff, independent review pass before dispatch.

title: Bound direct schema context to prevent model-budget exhaustion
description: The immutable public-baseline-v1-full archeology_scan_1:C1 attempt exhausted the per-turn Claude budget after 5 schema inspections and 5 SQL executions, consuming 1,114,427 tokens and USD 7.4942295 without an answer. The current schema search permits up to four whole tables / 64 KiB per call, and the accumulated conversation repeatedly re-bills those payloads. Implement the smallest general public-only retrieval/context bound that prevents this failure without question-specific routing or hidden/gold inputs; preserve competent schema discovery and C1-C3 fairness.
design: Trace-first, local change before architecture: inspect the five public schema results and reduce redundant/irrelevant context using a general deterministic bound or deduplication. Do not raise budgets, special-case archeology/question text, or weaken capture/custody. Preserve old failed attempt immutably.
acceptance_criteria: RED test reproduces bounded-search/context accumulation causing model-budget failure or payload excess; fix applies uniformly across databases/conditions, has deterministic limits and provenance, and does not use question IDs/hidden labels. archeology_scan_1:C1 public replay answers within the frozen attempt budget or the database is explicitly excluded with evidence. Focused/full direct tests and Ruff pass; independent code review clears; cost/token delta is recorded before full fan-out.
notes:
2026-08-28T17:40Z TDD: RED showed four matching whole tables permit repeated schema context growth. Minimal cross-database structural intervention caps schema retrieval at two whole-table matches while retaining the existing 64 KiB per-call guard. Replaying the five public archeology failure-trace retrieval queries mechanically reduced cumulative schema payload from 187,261 to 91,439 bytes (-51.2%) and stable-ID occurrences from 468 to 227. No question/database rules or hidden inputs. 506 focused direct tests and full 1,385-test suite pass; Ruff clean; independent review approved. Live replay2 at commit 3395421 ended refused/agent_refusal with no SQL/result: 732,563 tokens (-34.3%), USD 4.3204315 (-42.4%), 125.783s, 10 tools (6 schema/4 SQL), 4 DB queries, versus prior model_budget_error at 1,114,427 tokens/USD 7.4942295/131.972s/10 tools/5 queries. The intervention removes budget exhaustion but does not make this item answer; outcome remains FOLLOW UP / product tradeoff rather than a correctness KEEP.
First live incidence on the 16db continuation. cross_border_6 C1 captured failure_class=model_budget_error, failure_origin=evaluated_system, generation_outcome=errored, database_query_count=0, cost $3.82 (the most expensive attempt in the segment), latency 60.8s. Zero database queries with an exhausted budget on the schema-retrieval condition is the signature this bug describes: context spent on schema before a single query is issued.

Rate at 20:10Z is 1 of 11 captures (9%). If it holds across the 518-attempt continuation that is ~47 attempts concentrated in C1 and roughly $180 of the $2000 ceiling.

Classification is the load-bearing part and is a human-controlled surface, so flagging rather than changing. Attributing these to evaluated_system scores them as the system failing the question. If the cause is a harness-side unbounded schema context, the origin is arguably the harness, and under the rerun policy ('reruns require a demonstrable failure outside the evaluated system') reclassification would make these attempts rerunnable. The opposite reading is also defensible: the system was given a schema and managed its budget badly. This needs a human decision before scoring, not after seeing results.

Monitor now emits RUN-BUDGET-EXHAUSTION with a running rate on each occurrence, since the evaluated_system attribution means the infrastructure-failure filter does not catch them.
Rate correction (2026-08-28 20:00Z). The earlier "1 of 11 captures (9%), concentrated in C1" figure is withdrawn on both counts.

Measured on the live continuation run public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1 alone:

  cross_border_large/c1/cross_border_6-r1
  fake_account_large/c3/fake_account_19-r1  ($5.91)

Two corrections. (1) The failure is not confined to the schema-retrieval condition; the C3 occurrence rules out the condition-specific story the earlier note told. (2) Two events across three conditions supports neither a pattern claim nor a rate claim, so the ~47-attempt / ~$180 projection built on 9% is withdrawn rather than rescaled. The run finishes tonight with roughly 170 attempts per condition, which is when an incidence figure becomes reportable.

Cause of the bad number: the monitor pooled model_budget_error counts across every run root. Those roots hold ten runs, 207 captures from the parent worktree's earlier direct run alone, so both the numerator and the denominator mixed historical attempts with live ones. repeat within one question at n=3 attempts is also unremarkable at p~6% across 22

and whether C2 stays at zero once all four conditions have their ~170 attempts.

2. C2 has zero failures in 42 attempts. Expected under a common rate is about 2.3;

If both hold, the reading is that budget exhaustion is a property of the question's
schema breadth interacting with the scaffold, and that whatever C2's searchable HKB does
to schema access avoids the failure. That would make this a finding about scaffold
design rather than only a bug to bound, which is the kind of evidence the project is for.

I had been tracking model_budget_error only, because that is what this bead is about.

PREREGISTERED TEST, 22:00Z, registered at 220 of 518 captures before observing the rest.

organ_transplant_6 has now exhausted budget in all three conditions (c1, c2, c3), the
first question to fail everywhere it ran. Permutation test on the first 216 captures,
200k resamples holding the failure count fixed and redistributing over 213 attempts
across 71 fully-run questions:

Both reject independence. The reading is that budget exhaustion is a property of the
QUESTION, not the scaffold: c1 5, c2 1, c3 4 is a handful of hard questions surfacing
wherever they run, not three scaffold weaknesses. This supersedes every condition-level
story I told earlier today, including the C1-and-C3 pairing.

The p-values above are post-hoc; I found the pattern in the data before testing it. So
the test is now registered as a confirmatory one on the remaining ~300 captures:

  experiments/analysis/budget_clustering_test.py
  sha256 dac0aa86154453e02f6b528566ae0d010aaf18c1ac103e71d47cdfbd3e966994

  statistic     questions failing in >=2 of 3 conditions, among questions run in all 3

  threshold     one-sided p < 0.01
  rule          no substituted statistic after seeing the result

Consequence for this bead's fix, which is the actionable part. The proposed remedy is
bounding schema context, which is a scaffold-level intervention. If the driver is
question-level breadth, a uniform bound will not help the questions that actually fail,
and may cost accuracy on the ones that do not. Recommend the acceptance criteria be
re-examined against the confirmatory result before implementing, rather than building
the bound and discovering it misses.
PREREGISTERED TEST RESULT - NOT CONFIRMED

Run public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1 finished at 518/518. Ran

2026-08-28 22:00Z at 220 captures, sha256 dac0aa86154453e02f6b528566ae0d010aaf18c1ac103e71d47cdfbd3e966994):

The post-hoc pattern (budget exhaustion clusters by question rather than by
scaffold, P=0.0073/0.0053 in the first 216 captures) does not replicate on the
holdout at the registered threshold. The holdout carried 4 budget errors against

a fact about the test, not a reason to move the threshold. No statistic
substituted after seeing the result.

title: Round-2 attribution instrumentation batch (one schema boundary)
description:
The attribution items from the gve.3 audit that are not the field_kinds sidecar
(gve.3.1) and not the SQLSTATE schema bump (omni-benchmark-bfb). Each is telemetry
the sealed run wanted and did not have.

  - Fail open on UNKNOWN result types. Persist the raw payload as
    unscorable_pending instead of collapsing it into a generic failure, so a type
    the adapter has not met yet is a known gap rather than a silent wrong answer.
  - Retain plan bodies, trace payloads, and governed SQL under the dev tier. The
    sealed tier's retention rules are what forced the organ_transplant_large and
    mental_healths_large classification to be reconstructed by joining
    action-evidence SQL text to per-seq trace status (omni-benchmark-2j9).
  - Time-semantics features in wrong_answer_structure. Date-truncation and
    interval-boundary disagreements are currently indistinguishable from ordinary
    wrong answers.
  - Scorer-disagreement diff with dev-A adjudication. The two frozen scorers
    disagree on a known set of questions; nothing records why, per question.
  - Per-attempt dev-A mechanism annotation under a frozen codebook, published as
    counts only. The codebook must be frozen before the sample it labels, which is
    the correction D-207 made to the budget-clustering registration: commit the
    registration file before the data it governs so the attestation is
    git-attested rather than log-attested.
  - A harness-induced-failure row in the taxonomy. Roughly two thirds of the C1
    resource penalty in sealed-final-v6 is our own budget cap, not the model:
    model_budget_error alone is 33/31/22/0 across C1-C4, while budget plus rate
    limit is 46/46/38/0. The taxonomy currently gives the reader no way to see
    that separation.

Sequencing: every item that adds a field to an exact-set validated artifact rides
the same schema bump as bfb. Do not land them one at a time against the frozen
series; batch them into the round-2 series opener so there is exactly one version
boundary and one bridge round.
acceptance_criteria: All items land behind a single artifact-schema version boundary with tests; the dev-A mechanism codebook is committed before the sample it labels; the taxonomy separates harness-induced failures from model failures.

title: Emit compiler field_kinds as a sidecar attribution artifact
description:
semantic_bundle._table_dimensions builds a field_kinds map (source columns via
schema_value_kind, physical fields via physical_value_kind, derived fields from
the representation), uses it to drive coerce_numeric_references, and then returns
only (dimensions, names). The classification the compiler actually made is never
recorded, so no analysis can ask what kinds of fields C3 and C4 had available on
a given question.

Design constraint found during the gve.3 audit, do not skip it: the obvious
implementation, adding a field_kinds key to _bundle_manifest, is wrong. That
manifest is committed under semantic_models/public_baseline/*/bundle/manifest.json
and semantic_models/public_bundle/manifest.json, was deployed for the sealed run,
and was verified by exact readback. Adding a key changes bytes that are custody
evidence for a completed measurement, and the manifest carries schema_version 1
which several tests and the deploy path pin.

Correct shape: a sidecar artifact outside the bundle. Have _table_dimensions
return the map, carry it on SemanticBundle as an attribute that is not part of
files or manifest, and add a command that recompiles the committed specs and
writes a field-kinds artifact under experiments/analysis/. Recompilation from the
same inputs is deterministic, so the artifact can be produced for the frozen
series retroactively without a new run and without touching a deployed byte.

Do not land the return-value threading on its own. A returned value with no
consumer is placeholder code; land the producer and the consumer together.

Value: makes "which field kinds were available" a first-class attribution
variable for the round-2 analysis, and lets wrong_answer_structure separate a
type-coercion failure from a semantic one.
acceptance_criteria: A command recompiles the committed bundle specs and writes a field-kinds artifact; every byte under semantic_models/ is unchanged; tests cover the sidecar and assert the committed manifests still regenerate identically.
notes:
PLAN: Emit compiler field_kinds as a sidecar attribution artifact.

Goal: the classification semantic_bundle already computes for every modeled field
becomes a recorded, analyzable artifact, with zero change to any committed byte
under semantic_models/.

Approach:
1. semantic_bundle._table_dimensions returns (dimensions, names, field_kinds)
   instead of discarding the map it already builds.
2. SemanticBundle gains a third field, field_kinds: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
   keyed table_stable_id -> field name -> kind. It is not in files and not in
   manifest, so no published or deployed byte moves and manifest schema_version
   stays 1. _build_bundle collects the per-table maps. The two derived compilers
   (compile_e02_relationship_bundle, semantic_c5.compile_c5_tuned_bundle) pass
   the baseline map through explicitly; their added endpoint and injected aliases
   reuse the already classified source column name, so nothing is invented there.
3. Consumer, landed in the same change: experiments/analysis/semantic_field_kinds.py
   recompiles every committed spec set (config/archeology_scan_public_bundle.json
   plus the 18 semantic_models/public_baseline/*/bundle.spec.json) and writes
   experiments/analysis/semantic-field-kinds-v1.json. Per database and per view it
   emits dimension_field_kinds (fields the model can reference) separately from
   source_only_field_kinds (base columns that exist only as coercion inputs), plus
   per database and total counts by kind. Read only with respect to
   semantic_models; output goes to the path given by --output.
4. Register the artifact in docs/evidence-index.md and record the decision in
   docs/research-log.md.

Files to touch: src/omni_benchmark/semantic_bundle.py, src/omni_benchmark/semantic_c5.py,
experiments/analysis/semantic_field_kinds.py (new),
experiments/analysis/semantic-field-kinds-v1.json (new),
tests/test_semantic_field_kinds.py (new), tests/test_semantic_bundle.py,
tests/test_semantic_bundle_committed_artifacts.py, docs/evidence-index.md,
docs/research-log.md.

Tests:
- sidecar unit tests: field_kinds carries the expected kinds for a source column,
  a physical field, a numeric cast, and each derived representation; the map is
  absent from manifest and from every compiled file body.
- committed regeneration: extend the committed-artifact test so all 18
  public_baseline bundles, not only public_bundle, regenerate byte for byte with
  the manifest hash unchanged.
- analysis command: exact expected totals for the committed inputs, output written
  only to --output, and the emitted bytes carry no forbidden field name.

Risks:
- Manifest bytes are custody evidence for the sealed run. Mitigated by keeping
  field_kinds off both files and manifest and by the byte-for-byte test over all
  committed bundles.
- Artifact size: full per-field detail across 19 databases. Measure before
  committing; emit compact JSON and drop to counts only if it is unreasonable.
- Ambiguous source names are excluded from field_kinds by the existing
  len(stable_ids) == 1 guard, so a collided name is absent rather than wrong. The
  artifact reports the count so the gap is visible, not silent.

Out of scope: any change to bundle files, manifests, schema_version, or the
deployed models; classifying the extra aliases E02 and C5 materialize outside
_table_dimensions; wiring field kinds into wrong_answer_structure (a separate
consumer, gve.3.3).

Landed producer and consumer together.

Producer. SemanticBundle carries field_kinds as a third field, keyed
table_stable_id -> field name -> kind, outside files and manifest.
semantic_bundle_publication._build_bundle_artifacts reads only those two, so no
deployed or published byte moves and manifest schema_version stays 1.
_table_dimensions returns the map it already builds instead of discarding it.
compile_e02_relationship_bundle passes the baseline map through, because its
endpoint aliases reuse a source column name the baseline already classified.
compile_c5_tuned_bundle additionally classifies the columns
_inject_unrepresentable_fields synthesizes, which have no baseline entry; that
went slightly beyond the approved plan, which had assumed C5 aliases were also
pass-through.

Consumer. experiments/analysis/semantic_field_kinds.py recompiles all 18
committed spec sets (config/archeology_scan_public_bundle.json plus the 17
public_baseline/*/bundle.spec.json; the 18th public_baseline entry is
manifest.json, not a database) and writes
experiments/analysis/semantic-field-kinds-v1.json, 81 KB. Per view it separates
dimension_field_kinds, what the model can reference, from
source_only_field_kinds, base columns that exist only as coercion inputs.
Totals: 127 views, 599 published dimensions (317 numeric, 126 text, 97 other,
59 numeric_text), 1,186 source-only columns, 0 unclassified.
unclassified_dimension_field_count is the tripwire for the len(stable_ids) == 1
ambiguity exclusion; it is zero today and the artifact reports it so a future
gap is visible rather than silent. Each database record carries the SHA-256 of
its four public inputs.

Tests. tests/test_semantic_field_kinds.py hashes the whole semantic_models/
tree before and after a run and asserts it is unchanged, and asserts the
committed artifact is byte-identical to a fresh run.
tests/test_semantic_bundle_committed_artifacts.py gained a check that all 18
committed bundle manifests keep their exact key set and schema_version 1.
tests/test_semantic_bundle.py gained four sidecar tests including a
published-bytes guard; tests/test_semantic_c5.py gained one for the injected
column. No second baseline-regeneration loop was added:
tests/test_semantic_fanout_committed_artifacts.py:106 already regenerates all
17 baseline bundles byte for byte.

Docs. Artifact registered in docs/evidence-index.md with file SHA-256
1a9189a2e97fc0906fb470cd3da460ad02da33ce629fcdc2a3610ae7fa579866 and generator
SHA-256 cfd22cb576daf3ebce6260a4cff7dde378c875becfb57289137034126a363e7c.
Decision recorded as D-209 in docs/research-log.md.

Gate. Full suite: 2,251 passed, 3 skipped, coverage 82.23% against fail_under

tests/test_semantic_field_kinds.py, tests/test_semantic_bundle.py,

Done here: docs/protocol-amendment-dev-tier-draft.md, the two-tier custody proposal.
It is marked "proposal awaiting human approval, not in force", because custody rules
are a human-controlled surface. It names eight controls that carry over to the
development tier (both frozen scorers co-reported, the no-rerun rule, append-only

Also landed under this bead: two runtime reproducibility defects found while
auditing, written up as D-208.

The Claude CLI path was hardcoded to one person's home directory, which made the
direct arms unrunnable on any other machine. Now resolved through
OMNI_BENCHMARK_CLAUDE_BINARY with the SHA-256 pin untouched, so relocating the
binary relaxes nothing: a path whose bytes do not match the pin is still refused.

The trace schema version string had three independent copies. Both writers
hardcoded "trace-event-v2" while the validator compared the constant, so bumping
the constant would have made every run fail validation of its own artifacts at
write time. Both writers now import TRACE_SCHEMA_VERSION, and
tests/test_trace_schema_version_binding.py enforces single declaration plus a
tripwire on the current value. This is a precondition for the round-2 schema bump
that gve.3.3 and bfb depend on.

title: DECISION: authorize a phase-2 governed condition with measures and resolved grain
description:
PROPOSAL, needs operator authorization before any live action. D-197 authorized
exactly one further development condition, C5, and nothing else, so this bead is
a decision request, not work that can start.

QUESTION

Does a governed Omni deployment ever compose a query through the semantic model,
or is the raw-SQL rewrite path unconditional?

WHAT C5 SETTLED AND WHAT IT DID NOT

C5 published a view for every public table (47 to 63 per database against the
mechanical baseline's 6 to 11) and a join for every foreign key that passes the
conservative cardinality contract. Accuracy doubled on the identical 136-attempt
frame, 18 of 136 against 9 of 136 official, at roughly two-thirds the median
token cost. The rewrite rate did not move at all: 134 of 134 parseable C5
attempts carry rewriteSql, none declares a join through the model, and
join_via_map is zero. Across six governed arms the count is 661 of 661.

So relationship coverage is ruled out as the binding constraint. What remains
untested is the one ingredient C5 deliberately excluded: measures, which require
grain resolution, and which are the only model element that makes an aggregate
question expressible as a compiled query rather than as SQL.

DESIGN SKETCH

A phase-2 condition identical to C5 except that it publishes measures on topics
whose grain can be resolved from public schema structure alone, with the same
no-guess rule the compiler already applies. Same public inputs, same custody,
both frozen scorers, dev-A only, one generation, no promotion path.

The readout is the query-path tally, not accuracy. If the rewrite rate stays at
100% with measures present, the fallback is unconditional, PF-016 hardens from a
coverage-conditional finding into an unconditional one, and the product fix is
observability and enforcement rather than model completeness. If any composed
query appears, the 46.9% grain-deferral rate is the constraint and the
compilation pipeline is where to invest.

Accuracy would be reported but is secondary: this is a mechanism probe.

RELATED

Supersedes the coverage-conditional-versus-unconditional framing in
omni-benchmark-bpk with a concrete design. See PF-016 in docs/product-findings.md
and D-205 in docs/research-log.md.

title: Mechanism probe: is Omni's governed enforcement coverage-conditional or unconditional?
description:
Mechanism probe: does the Omni governed endpoint compile when a compiled path
exists, or does it take the rewrite path unconditionally?

MOTIVATION

Frozen C4 measured 135/135 governed queries with rewriteSql true, aiGenerated
true, hand-authored SQL in userEditedSQL, generated_sql null, and zero declared
join paths. The deployed model published no joins and no measures, so no
compiled path existed for any cross-table or aggregate question. Two mechanisms
fit that observation equally well and the study cannot separate them:

  A. Coverage-conditional. The product compiles when the model supports it and
     silently falls back to agent-authored SQL when it does not.
  B. Unconditional. The product always takes the rewrite path, and the empty
     model merely made that invisible.

E02 is a hint toward B (declared joins live on 61 of 114 topics, all 131
captured semantic queries still rewrites) but is INCONCLUSIVE by our own
complete-136 rule and cannot carry the claim.

The distinction changes the product finding materially. Under A, C4 is our
coverage failure and the governed path works when fed. Under B, "governed"
means field vocabulary only and composition is always the agent's, which is a
stronger and differently actionable finding.

DESIGN

One database. Three model variants on isolated livesqlbench-* branches, built
from the C5 compiler entry point with flags. Hold question wording, database,
harness, and posted request shape constant; vary only model coverage.

  V0  mechanical view surface (6-11 views), no joins, no measures
  V1  full view surface, all passing FK joins, no measures
  V2  full view surface, all passing FK joins, one trivial single-table measure

V2 is the decisive arm. A single-table count or sum has no grain ambiguity, so
the compiler builds it without guessing. It is the one case where an
unambiguous compiled path provably exists.

PROBE QUESTIONS

Six questions invented from the public schema. NOT benchmark questions, no gold,
no scoring, no correctness recorded. Each shaped so a compiled path would
trivially satisfy it.

  Q1  single-table count                       compilable in V0, V1, V2
  Q2  single-table filtered count on a compiled dimension   V0, V1, V2
  Q3  two-table count across one declared FK   V1, V2 only
  Q4  the exact V2 measure, asked in the measure's own words   V2 only
  Q5  Q4 paraphrased                           V2 only
  Q6  three-hop join                           V1, V2 only

READOUT

Per attempt, from the query object only: rewriteSql, generated_sql non-null,
join_via_map non-empty, routed topic, resolved fields. No scorer run. No
accuracy. 18 generations total.

INTERPRETATION, FIXED BEFORE RUNNING

  V2 Q4 returns a compiled query        -> mechanism A, coverage-conditional
  V2 Q4 returns rewriteSql true         -> mechanism B, unconditional
  outcome varies by question shape      -> routing threshold, more informative
                                           than either clean answer

CUSTODY AND AUTHORIZATION

Tier 1. Public schema and public HKB only. No questions from any partition, no
gold, no hidden annotations, no dev-B, no test data, no correctness. Isolated
livesqlbench-* branches only. Records append-only. Retries permitted under a
new run ID per Tier 1.

SEQUENCING

Run after C5 pass 5 lands cleanly, to avoid branch contention on the shared
deployment path and because a clean C5 deployment is the harder artifact to
get. As of 2026-08-31 v6 verified all 16 databases, so this is unblocked on
that count.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE

Three variants, one database, six questions. Do not expand unless the readout
is genuinely ambiguous. CLAUDE.md: evaluation apparatus must not displace
evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: 18 attempts captured across V0/V1/V2 with per-attempt rewriteSql, generated_sql, join_via_map, routed topic and resolved fields recorded in an append-only artifact; a written verdict of mechanism A, mechanism B, or a described routing threshold; no scorer run, no correctness recorded, no non-public inputs used.
notes:
C5 narrows this but does not close it. The docs-idiomatic deployment published a
view for every table and a join for every qualifying foreign key, so a compiled
cross-table path existed on most topics. All 134 parseable C5 attempts still took
the rewrite path and none declared a join, which rules out mechanism A in its
join-coverage form: the product did not compile when joins became available.

What survives is a narrower version of A, conditional on measures rather than on
joins, since C5 published none and an aggregate question has no compiled
expression without one. Separating that from B requires the phase-2 condition
proposed in omni-benchmark-w5x.

Evidence: experiments/analysis/governed-query-path-tally-v1.json, 661 of 661
parseable attempts on the rewrite path across six governed arms. Recorded as
PF-016 and D-205.

description:

parity as an open blocker. Measurement and shipped code falsify all three.

(`omni_result_adapter.py:434-479`) requires status `PLANNED`, empty
`missing_fields` and `invalid_calculations`, and exact ordered field agreement
between `model_job.fields` and the semantic query's `fields`; `_typed_cell`
(`:497-543`) converts strictly by declared `data_type` and never infers type
from string appearance. Typed cells persist in the hash-bound sidecar and

`57d45346de0a98384207d350f163dfcf812e677cf3719b4a3008b5e0f3f222d8`; sensitivity

title: Elevate C4 contract-failure reliability fixes to first-class interventions
description: 34 of 136 scoreable C4 attempts ended in a semantic-layer or system-contract failure (refusals, system errors) rather than in a wrong answer that reflects a real modeling gap. A general reliability fix that converts these refused or system-error outcomes into scoreable answers has a larger expected accuracy gain than most individual semantic-modeling changes, because it recovers attempts that never got a fair shot at being scored correct in the first place. Several such fixes have already landed and shown effect, including the result adapter and typed-row handling. This bead is to formally elevate contract-failure reliability work to a first-class intervention family, tracked alongside the existing E02/E03/E04 intervention families, with the same generality constraints that apply to those: fixes must be general improvements to the harness/system-contract handling, not question-specific patches, and must be validated the same way other interventions are.
close_reason: Cancelled unrun by the documented hard stop after E02; no further reliability intervention is authorized.

comments.author: sjarmak
comments.text:
Specified E05-reliability as a first-class intervention family. Deliverable: docs/c4-reliability-intervention-family.md. No code, registration, or committed doc was modified; experiments/planned-dev-a-interventions-v1.json is untouched.

TAXONOMY of the 34 terminal evaluated-system failures (D-155 recovery v5, aggregate-only):
- A. UNKNOWN planner result type on a selected field: 32 (94%). Evaluated-system surface.
- B. Completed job, no parseable generated query: 1.
- C. Persistent plan rejection: 1.
- D. Recovered by single-shot result replay: 11 (these are why 45 capture failures became 34 terminal, not part of the 34).
Capture-time labels were 34 unsupported-type / 10 response-contract / 1 transport; the per-attempt mapping to final class is not derivable from published aggregates. The composition cross-checks against the independent structural pass: exactly the 32 class-A records carry parseable governed SQL, the two singletons do not.

LANDED vs REMAINING:
Every landed fix is on the harness side, not the evaluated system: D-121 (9526505) preview/action parsing; D-132 selected-field vs dependency-field validation; D-155 boolean/empty-string/typed-null replay; D-168 (d18ce32) completed-job contract semantics; D-169 (34b7812) unsupported types preserved as a distinct outcome; D-170 (8b0c739) already-returned JSON rows bound after preview mismatch. Those converted 11 attempts to scored and made the rest classifiable. None is an accuracy intervention and none should be reported as one.
Remaining loss is entirely class A and it is on the evaluated-system side. No further adapter change can recover it: c4_result_recovery fails closed on UNKNOWN because value-based type inference changes comparison semantics, which D-132 rejected deliberately.

MECHANISM: semantic_bundle._derived_dimension emits compiled derived fields with label, description, sql, ai_context and no declared output type, so the product must infer the type of a derived expression. The compiler already holds what it needs: the mapping records a boolean/categorical/numeric representation class, and semantic_numeric already classifies public declared column types. Supported result types are BOOLEAN, DATE, JSON, NUMBER, STRING, TIMESTAMP, YESNO.

SPEC: E05-reliability declares an explicit output type on every compiled semantic field from the representation class plus public declared column types only, and defers to searchable context when those do not jointly determine one supported type. No value-based, question-based, gold-based, or failure-based inference. Generality constraint binds every rule: no database name, question, or label. Evaluation path matches E02: all 154 scheduled, 18 fixed exclusions, promotion on all 136 answerable, deployment set derived from the committed answerable schedule. Cheap offline precondition first: count how many of the 32 UNKNOWN failures selected a compiled derived field vs a physical field, using field-kind metadata on the immutable v8 records. Under 16 means the compiler mechanism does not carry the class and E05 is INCONCLUSIVE with zero live attempts spent. Promotion adds a terminal-failure-vector report; a wrong_answer to refused_or_error move is a regression even at flat accuracy.

EXPECTED VALUE: ambient scored rate is 9/102 = 8.82%; one answer is 0.74 points; the gate is 2 answers = 1.47 points. Half-conversion yields about 1.5 expected answers, which is UNDER the gate. Full class-A conversion yields about 2.8 answers, 6.62% to 8.69%, a 2.07-point and 31% relative gain, above the gate any single modeling candidate must clear. Error queries average 2.88 relations vs 2.62 wrong and 1.67 correct, so converted attempts may score below ambient and the direct argument is real but not decisive.
The stronger case is measurement capacity. The 34 are insensitive to every modeling change, because the contract fails downstream of the semantic query an intervention alters. They cap accuracy at 102/136 = 75%, shrink every other gate to 102 informative attempts, and absorb small true gains inside the error class. Restoring class A raises the informative denominator by 31% at no additional live cost, which makes E05 a multiplier on E01-E04 rather than a competitor for the same budget, and argues for sequencing it early rather than ranking it on projected accuracy alone.

Bead left OPEN; execution follows in the optimization loop.

comments.text:
Harness-versus-product attribution analysis written to docs/c4-failure-attribution.md (aggregate public evidence only; no private, gold, or per-question data read).

VERIFIED IN SOURCE
1. semantic_bundle._derived_dimension (lines 587-606) emits label/description/sql/ai_context and no type. Confirmed.
2. The omission is broader than the bead states: _physical_dimension (571-584) declares no type either. No field of any kind in any compiled bundle declares an output type.
3. Strongest fact for the harness reading: the compiler computes the type and discards it. field_kinds at line 1142 maps representation to other/text/numeric in the same loop that emits the field document without it; physical_value_kind does the same for physical fields.
4. The harness is at the correct boundary. omni_result_adapter.py:475 and c4_result_recovery.py:298 fail closed on UNKNOWN; D-132 rejected value-based inference deliberately. No adapter change can recover a class-A attempt.
5. The UNKNOWN label is a replay-time property. recover_c4_source calls plan_query fresh (line 278). Concordance with the 34 capture-time unsupported-type labels is good, identity is not established, and D-155 says the per-attempt mapping is not derivable from published aggregates.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED
PF-014 is the single field-level observation (ETF yield_to_expense_ratio). Everything else about class A is an aggregate count. The causal link from "no declared type" to UNKNOWN is untested; E05's own precondition is unrun. The bead's phrasing "the mechanism is OUR compiler" overstates the record. Overstating our own culpability is also a defensibility failure, because it licenses an unfalsified implicit claim that Omni would have scored higher.

NEW FINDING THAT REFRAMES THE MECHANISM
omni_attempt.py:166-173 sets generated_sql: None for every C4 attempt, so the C4 structural aggregate is computed entirely from generated_query["userEditedSQL"] (D-172 states this). 133 of 136 attempts carried one, including 32 of 34 errors. The deployed topics declare joins: {} and no measures, so a query compiled from the model cannot reference two distinct tables through a declared join path. Yet 20/32 error and 50/92 wrong queries are multi-relation. Either the agent used the raw-SQL path, or the planner resolved undeclared cross-table access. Either way, a compile-time type on a modeled field may not be the mechanism for class A. Confounder stated in the doc: relation_count counts CTE references, aliased self-joins, and subquery sources, so multi-relation prevalence is an upper bound on cross-table access, which also qualifies the RESULTS.md and failure-taxonomy structural claims.

ATTRIBUTION
Class A (32): genuinely disputed, both readings argued. Class B (1) and C (1): product, weakly contestable. Class D (11): harness, already corrected, not in the 34. The 18 loader exclusions: benchmark infrastructure, already outside the denominator. Whatever is decided about class A, 94 percent of the block turns on one question.

The endorsed reading is that the type contract between a programmatic model author and the semantic layer is under-specified. Our compiler declared no type because nothing required one and validation confirmed nothing was missing. The product required one only at query planning time and reported its absence as a value rather than a diagnosable error. Neither side violated a stated contract because none exists. That reading survives the gaps above; the single-cause readings do not.

SENSITIVITY (all descriptive, none a corrected estimate)
136 frame: 9/136 = 6.6 percent. Scoreable-result subset: 9/102 = 8.8 percent, identical under both frozen scorers.
122 four-condition intersection: C4 5/122 = 4.1 percent, C1 7.4, C2 23.8, C3 13.1.
Symmetric exclusion of each condition's own non-answers on 122: C1 10.1, C2 24.2, C3 17.8, C4 5.7. Ordering unchanged.
Non-answer rates on the identical 122: C4 27.9, C1 27.0, C3 26.2, C2 1.6. C4's non-answer rate is not anomalous, which is the fact that stops the 34 being read as unique governed-path fragility, and it is the reason excluding non-answers for C4 alone is the wrong comparison.
Bounds: ambient-rate conversion of all 34 gives 8.8 percent on 136 and 5.7 percent on 122, closing 1.6 of the 19.7-point gap to C2. All-correct ceiling is 31.6 and 32.0 percent, a logical bound only. Error queries average 2.875 relations against 2.620 wrong and 1.667 correct, so ambient is more likely an upper bound than a central estimate for that subset.
Artifact a reader will find: narrowing 136 to 122 removes 4 of 9 correct, 10 of 93 wrong, and none of the 34 errors, which is why 6.6 becomes 4.1.

RECOMMENDED REPORT LANGUAGE
Section 8 of the doc gives drafted replacements for RESULTS.md executive-summary findings 2 and 5, a new paragraph in section 5, three new Limitations bullets, a sharpened product recommendation 5 adding the validation-time half, and a framed "what the 34 do and do not support" block. Headline stays 9/136 = 6.6 percent, never an exclusion-based number. RESULTS.md was not edited.

BEFORE ANY MECHANISM CLAIM REACHES RESULTS.md
1. Run the E05 precondition: how many of the 32 selected a compiled derived field versus a physical field. Offline, aggregate.
2. Count userEditedSQL divergence against declared fields, shape only. Offline, aggregate.
3. Probe whether Omni accepts a declared field type at all and still plans UNKNOWN. Tier 1, public only. This is the one assumption in the harness reading that has never been checked; if it fails, that reading collapses.

Also flagged: the Disposition column in docs/c4-reliability-intervention-family.md section 2 reads as an attribution when it is a scoring disposition. If that table reaches RESULTS.md the column needs renaming.

Offline mechanism measurements run. Full writeup in docs/c4-mechanism-measurements.md; analyzer in experiments/analysis/c4_mechanism_measurements.py with tests in tests/test_c4_mechanism_measurements.py. Aggregate output SHA-256 56df0ab4d82e9d45ba3ef6296a473d9d6733b925835ec071ae6cd98f26d9053f. Custody-verified against official score 57d45346... and recovery manifest 5d6ff474.... Aggregate only, no identities emitted, nothing committed, HEAD untouched.

VERDICT: E05's precondition is NOT met. It is measurable and measured, not blocked.

CHECK 1, E05 precondition.
Class A is 31 attempts, not 32. The recovery manifest at the pinned digest holds 31 omni_unknown_result_type, 2 omni_query_plan_rejected, 1 omni_completed_job_contract_invalid. The 32/1/1 split in this bead, in docs/c4-reliability-intervention-family.md section 2, and in docs/c4-failure-attribution.md is wrong. Terminal total of 34 is unchanged.

Those 31 attempts select 130 field references. Provenance against the compiled bundles: 8 compiled derived (6.2%), 15 compiled physical (11.5%), 53 query-local CTE or alias names the attempt's own SQL defines (40.8%), 23 schema columns the bundle does not declare (17.7%), 20 names matching no bundle dimension and no schema column (15.4%), 8 Omni count built-in, 3 references to unpublished view identifiers.

By attempt: 6 of 31 contain at least one compiled derived field, 1 more contains a physical one only, 24 of 31 contain no compiled bundle field of any kind, 0 select derived fields exclusively. Since no artifact records which field carried UNKNOWN (the recovery manifest keeps only plan_sha256, traces are metadata-only), the true derived count lies in [0, 6]. The precondition target of 16 is above the ceiling by a factor of 2.7.

Base rates for context: at least one derived field appears in 0/9 correct, 6/93 wrong, 7/34 terminal failures, 6/31 class A. The association points the E05 direction; the absolute count kills the mechanism.

Note this also defeats the broader "declare a type on every emitted field" version: derived plus physical together reach only 7 of 31.

CHECK 2, SQL path shape.
generated_sql is None on 136 of 136, confirming omni_attempt.py:166-173. userEditedSQL is present on 135 of 136 (9/9 correct, 93/93 wrong, 33/34 error), of which 133 parse. The "133 carried userEditedSQL, including 32 of 34 errors" line in docs/c4-failure-attribution.md section 4 conflates presence with parseability.

The multi-relation puzzle resolves to the raw-SQL escape path. All 135 semantic queries carry rewriteSql true with hand-authored SQL text. Zero declare a join path in join_via_map. 62 of the 133 parseable queries reference two or more distinct non-CTE sources with join_via_map empty (2 correct, 41 wrong, 19 error). 17 have a `table` value naming a CTE their own SQL defines. The planner did not resolve undeclared cross-table access; the agent wrote CTEs and explicit JOINs over topic references in SQL text.

Consequence: what the planner failed to type is predominantly the output columns of agent-authored SQL, not fields the compiler emitted. A compile-time field type cannot attach to an alias the agent invented in a CTE.

RELATION-COUNT CONFOUNDER.
Corrected count removes WITH-bound names and collapses aliases to base relation names.
Correct (n=9): mean 1.667 -> 1.333, multi-relation 2/9 -> 2/9.
Wrong (n=92): 2.620 -> 1.826, 50/92 -> 41/92.
Error (n=32): 2.875 -> 2.000, 20/32 -> 19/32.
Class A (n=30): 2.900 -> 2.033, 19/30 -> 18/30.
Correct-to-wrong gap falls 0.953 -> 0.493 (48.3% reduction); correct-to-error 1.208 -> 0.667 (44.8%). Direction and ordering unchanged, magnitude roughly halves. CTE use is itself outcome-correlated (2/9, 40/92, 16/32), so the published metric partly measured query elaboration.
The published means and multi-relation counts reproduce RESULTS.md section 5 exactly under the original definition, which is the check that this analyzer reads the same records.
Join-presence figures survive the confounder: of 41 wrong queries with a join, 39 join two or more non-CTE sources; all 18 error joins do. No restatement needed there.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS INSTEAD.
Class A mechanism statement that fits all 31: the planner reported UNKNOWN for output columns of agent-authored SQL that the semantic model does not define, and the harness fails closed on UNKNOWN. Consistent with PF-014 and PF-006. Attribution between harness and product is not settled; the disputed surface moves from "our compiler under-declared its fields" to "the product plans rewritten SQL it cannot type, and neither side specifies the result contract over it". Section 6.3 of the attribution doc survives; section 6.1's first bullet is true about the code and largely irrelevant to these 31 attempts.

The Tier 1 type-declaration acceptance probe (section 6.4(3)) is now lower value: even if Omni accepts and honors a declared type, it reaches at most 7 of 31.
