title: Add cheap dev-A subset screens before full-eval promotion runs
description: Each optimization iteration in the autoresearch loop currently costs a 16-database deploy plus a full 136-attempt dev-A run plus freeze and scoring, which caps the MVP to roughly 2-4 KEEP/REVERT cycles given time and budget constraints. Dev-A is adaptively reusable, and only a KEEP decision actually requires the full eligible dev-A comparison for a valid protocol-compliant result; weak candidates are being promoted through the full expensive pipeline before being rejected. Design a small, fixed screening subset of dev-A that can cheaply reject weak candidates before committing to a full promotion run, without changing what counts as a valid KEEP determination. This is protocol-compatible as designed: it only needs to gate which candidates proceed to the full run, not replace the full run's role in the KEEP decision, so no protocol change is required. The expected payoff is more optimization iterations within the same MVP budget.
close_reason: Cancelled unrun by the documented hard stop after E02; subset-screening framework is outside the submission MVP.

comments.author: sjarmak
comments.text:
Design delivered: docs/dev-a-screening-design.md (new file, working tree only, not committed).

Population. Answerable dev-A frame = 154 scheduled minus the 18 conformance-excluded identities = 136 over 16 databases, 71/65 high_level. mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large drop out entirely. archeology_scan_large and cybermarket_pattern_large stay in: public-baseline-exclusions-v1.json is scoped public-only-c1-c3-baseline and does not apply to the governed C4 path.

Selection. n=32, the top of the allowed band, because every leg of the rule is power-limited and 4 extra attempts are negligible against the 104 a rejection saves. Algorithm database_high_level_sha256_screen_v1: exactly 2 per database; 1 from each high_level stratum where both are non-empty, otherwise 2 from the single non-empty stratum; within a stratum, order ascending by hex SHA-256(seed, 0x1f, database, high_level, instance_id). Equal allocation beats proportional here because the population is near-uniform (13 of 16 databases hold 9 to 11) and equal weight matches the generality objective. Resulting composition is fixed before any digest: 17 high_level true, 15 false (53.1% versus the population's 52.2%). Public metadata only; no outcome artifact is opened by the generator, asserted in the test.

Decision rule. Four gates, reject if any trips. (1) declared mechanism fires on 0 of 32; (2) any regression-suite capability the parent held is lost; (3) refused plus system-error outcomes >= 14 of 32; (4) 0 correct of 32 under both frozen scorers, when the accuracy leg is operative.

Error-rate leg trade-off at the 25.0% C4 baseline rate (34/136): threshold 14 gives 1.6% false rejection and 0.81 power against a doubled error rate; 13 gives 3.8%/0.89; 15 gives 0.6%/0.70. Chose 14.

Accuracy leg trade-off at 6.6% baseline: P(0 correct of 32) is 11.3% at baseline, 3.4% at 10%, 1.2% at 13%, 0.6% at 15%. So the floor discards a genuinely doubled candidate about 1 time in 80 and a baseline-equivalent candidate about 1 time in 9; the risk sits on candidates that could not have produced KEEP evidence anyway. Combined with the error leg: 12.7% false rejection for a baseline-identical candidate, 2.7% at 13% true accuracy. Stated plainly in the doc: 32 questions cannot separate 6.6% from 9%, so the rule contains no "fewer correct than baseline" comparison. It is a signs-of-life floor, not a superiority test.

Operativeness. After membership freeze the loop records, once, how many subset questions the baseline answers correctly (hypergeometric expectation 2.1, P(0)=8.2%, P(<=1)=32.8%). If that count is 0 or 1 the accuracy leg is declared non-operative for -v1 and only legs 1 and 2 apply. It depends on the baseline only, never a candidate, so declaring it at freeze is not a post-hoc escape. Rejection is terminal: no re-screening, or an 11% false-reject rate becomes a selection procedure against 32 questions.

Cost. Screen 32 versus a promotion run of 136 scored (154 scheduled). Saves 104 per rejection (76.5%), 122 against the scheduled frame (79.2%); costs 32 overhead per passing candidate (23.5%). Break-even pass rate 76.5%. Total for k candidates at pass fraction q is 32k + 136qk, ratio 0.235 + q. Worked cases: 6 candidates with 2 passing costs 464 versus 816, saving 352 attempts or 2.6 full runs; 6 with 5 passing costs 7% more than not screening. Screening does not save the 16-database deploy, since the subset covers all 16; a database-restricted screen would save deploy cost but cannot see database-specific regressions and biases against generality, so it is rejected. No published per-attempt C4 cost exists; the only reference is the $1.48-$1.84 C1-C3 band, which is not a C4 estimate, so convert using the candidate's own observed attempt mean.

Protocol compatibility, no change proposed. The KEEP gate is untouched: EVALUATION_PROTOCOL.md still requires a complete 154-question dev-A evaluation plus generality/regression/complexity rationale, and acceptance_policy.keep_requires_complete_dev_a_run stays true. The screen only filters and orders candidates that have not reached the gate; it produces no KEEP and is never KEEP evidence. It instantiates autoresearch.md step 4's prespecified slice, replacing a per-experiment declaration with one standing frozen slice, which is stronger because a per-experiment slice can drift. It does not hit the rejected pattern "acceptance based on a favorable subset" because it never accepts. Adaptive reuse is already permitted for dev-A and the subset opens no new data access; reject-only plus terminal rejection are the overfitting controls, and every KEEP is still computed on the full frame containing the 32. No dev-B, test, or hidden-annotation contact. Ledger: screen results append before the full run launches or the candidate is abandoned, recorded as REVERT or ARCHIVE with evaluation_scope screen_subset, own immutable run IDs, rerun policy unchanged. A screen rejection counts toward the 4-consecutive-non-KEEP review trigger.

Artifacts. Membership file config/conditions/dev-a-screen-subset-v1.json (committed), kind dev-a-screen-subset, schema_version 1, holding algorithm, baseline_reference, counts, decision_rule thresholds, distributions, instance_ids, quotas, scope, and sources with the eligible-manifest / dev_a_ids / exclusions SHA-256s cross-checked against dev-a-scorer-conformance-exclusions-v1.json. Membership and thresholds live under one hash so a proposal that records it has pinned both. Generator src/omni_benchmark/dev_a_screen_subset.py, CLI scripts/make_dev_a_screen_subset.py, byte-identical regeneration test tests/test_dev_a_screen_subset.py. Seed convention omni-livesqlbench-<artifact-slug>-v<N>, following D-054's omni-livesqlbench-c1-retrieval-sensitivity-v1; here omni-livesqlbench-dev-a-screen-subset-v1. A revision ships as -v2 with a new seed alongside -v1; the existing file is never edited.

Membership file deliberately not created. It gets generated in the loop under the committed seed before the first screened candidate produces any outcome. Bead left open for that execution.

Open items for the loop: generate -v1 and record its SHA-256 in the first screening proposal; compute baseline_reference right after freeze and publish whether the accuracy leg is operative; add evaluation_scope to the decision record.

title: Wrong-answer is the dominant failure class (245 of 366 scored) and has no owner
description:
From public-direct-baseline-dev-a-scores-v1, dev-A, official Soft EX:

  wrong_answer       245
  refused_or_error    67
  correct             54

The direct comparators mostly produce runnable SQL that returns the wrong result.
Per condition, wrong answers are C1 80, C2 91, C3 74 out of 122 scoreable.

The two open failure beads together cover 67 of 366 scored attempts:
omni-benchmark-dx3 (refusal, 80 captures) and dih.5.4.2.4.4.2.2.2 (model budget,
17 captures). The largest class by a factor of three has no bead.

Scope: characterize why runnable SQL returns wrong results. Candidate axes, to be
tested rather than assumed - join grain and fan-out, aggregation level, null and
filter semantics, ambiguous entity resolution, and the representability gap
already recorded for business definitions that cannot be compiled into executable
semantic objects without cardinality/grain/identity information.

Do this on dev-A only. Any intervention must be classified for generality before
it is made; question-specific changes are prohibited.

Note the accuracy ceiling this implies: at C2 23.8% [16.2, 31.3] the headroom is
almost entirely in this class, so it is where any real gain has to come from.
close_reason: Bounded dev-A characterization complete; any causal intervention test remains under the preregistered ei0.4 experiment sequence.

title: Refusal (no_answer_insufficient_context) is the dominant never-queried mode; needs its own bead
description:
Split out of omni-benchmark-dih.5.4.2.4.4.2.2.2, which is titled for unbounded
direct schema context causing model-budget exhaustion.

At full n on public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1 (518 captures):

  no_answer_insufficient_context   80   c1:37 c2:3  c3:40
  model_budget_error               17   c1:7  c2:3  c3:7

63 attempts issued zero database queries: 51 refusals, 12 budget exhaustions.
Refusal is roughly five times more common than the class the P0 bead is named
for, and the near-absence in C2 (3 of 80) says it tracks what reference material
the condition exposes, not the token budget.

These are different mechanisms with different fixes. Bounding schema context
addresses budget exhaustion; it does not address a model that reads the available
context and concludes it cannot answer. Keeping both on one bead was hiding the
larger of the two.

Scope here: characterize why C1 and C3 refuse where C2 does not, and whether the
refusal is correct behavior (the reference genuinely lacks what is needed) or
premature. Note that under Soft EX a refusal and a wrong answer both score zero,
so refusal is not rewarded by the frozen scorers even where it is the better
engineering behavior.

Blocked on omni-benchmark-2j9: 19 of the 80 refusals are on the two databases
with no queryable data tables, where refusal is the correct response to an empty
environment and must not be counted as a system property.

comments.author: sjarmak
comments.text:
C4 query-path disclosure investigation. Full findings in docs/c4-query-path-disclosure.md (new, untracked). Aggregate-only; no runs/ read, no gold, no identifiers, HEAD unchanged at 94cc0d9.

WHO CHOSE THE REWRITE PATH: Omni's agent, on every attempt. The harness never writes rewriteSql, userEditedSQL, join_via_map, or aiGenerated; zero hits anywhere under src/. The C4 prompt is the bare {question}. submit_job posts exactly modelId, progressWebhookEnabled false, prompt, branchId (omni_cli.py:193-208). Managed agent instructions are not_exposed_by_omni. The harness passes Omni's returned query back verbatim to plan_query and run_query_json; the only mutation sets modelId.

WAS A NON-REWRITE PATH AVAILABLE: not for cross-table access. Deployed topics emit joins {} with no measures (semantic_bundle.py:630-645, joins_generated False). No declared join path or measure existed to compile. For the 62 multi-relation attempts the rewrite path was the only option. The 73 single-relation attempts took it anyway, which is an unobservable product default. Classification: not a scaffold defect. There is no harness lever; steering the agent with prompt text would be a benchmark-specific intervention on the evaluated system.

DISCLOSED ANYWHERE: no. The finding exists only in docs/c4-mechanism-measurements.md and this bead, both untracked. Inaccurate published claims, ranked by severity: methodology.md:63 "Production harness enforces semantic compilation/validation" (most directly falsified); methodology.md:331-333 same; harness-disclosure.md:32 "Semantic query/objects compiled through Omni; generated SQL captured only if exposed" (not compiled, and the SQL was captured, in userEditedSQL); EVALUATION_PROTOCOL.md:212 "Enforced production harness"; the "Production-governed Omni" query-path row repeated at RESULTS.md:100, README.md:35, report-draft-v2.md:33; report-draft-v2.md:368 "the shape-only check that would resolve it is offline and has not been run" (it was run); RESULTS.md:343-350 relation aggregates with no source note. Notable pattern: C4 minus C3 is hedged in nine places, always on model and scaffold parity, never on the query path.

SEALED ARM: same behavior expected, established from committed configuration without touching the run. sealed_omni_factory.py:33-35 pins the identical condition, prompt, and instruction paths and raises if anything else is named. freeze-b-input.json and sealed-omni-semantic-model-set-v1.json both bind deployment public-baseline-v13-20260829 with per-database model hashes matching the dev arm. Same probe type and same write_c4_attempt. Prediction, not measurement.

C3 VERSUS C4, WHAT SURVIVES: still different are the agent (pinned claude-opus-5 under our scaffold versus Omni's unobservable managed agent), field resolution (C4 writes Omni dialect and Omni expands HKB-backed derived dimensions at rewrite time; C3 inlines them by hand), the execution engine and result contract (source of all 34 terminal failures), and the accessible surface. No longer different: who composes the query, and join and aggregation semantics. Both arms are an agent authoring SQL over the same compiled bundle, with byte-identical prompts.

WAS THE SEMANTIC MODEL USED: yes, as a vocabulary, not as a compiler, and this is the part that is more favorable than the headline. Input side, 1310 dollar-brace tokens across 135 SQL bodies: 315 resolve to compiled physical dimensions, 82 to compiled HKB-backed derived dimensions, 382 to undeclared schema columns, 249 unattributable bare tokens. 134 of 135 bodies use the reference syntax at all, 126 name a compiled view, 109 (80.7%) reference at least one compiled dimension, 39 (28.9%) reference at least one HKB-backed derived dimension, 26 (19.3%) reference none. Compiled counts are lower bounds. Output side, 518 selected field references: 58 compiled physical, 17 compiled derived, 443 not compiled; 0 of 135 attempts select exclusively compiled fields and 97 select none. The model is used heavily on the way in and barely at all on the way out, which is exactly what a raw-SQL rewrite produces and why the planner had output columns it could not type.

RECOMMENDATION: disclose and reinterpret. Not a defect, so do not patch. Restate C4 minus C3 as a contrast between two agent-authored SQL conditions differing in agent, dialect, accessible surface, and execution contract. Exact replacement language for all seven documents is in section 6 of the new doc. Cost is edits to published docs plus the framing loss: the study can no longer claim it isolated semantic-layer query composition.

Second option, for the optimized arm only since the sealed arm is hash-bound and nearly complete: declare joins and measures in the deployed model and report untuned versus optimized as a measured contrast on whether Omni's agent changes path. Scientifically the strongest move, largest cost, touches semantic_bundle.py, must be general not database-specific, and proves nothing about agent behavior on its own.

Third and cheap: a Tier 1 public-only probe on one public database with a declared join, checking whether the returned query carries join_via_map or still rewrites. De-risks option two for one deployment and one prompt.

Separate small defect worth fixing in the optimized arm: omni_attempt.py:171 hard-codes generated_sql null while the executed SQL sits in generated_query.userEditedSQL, so an auditor looks in an empty field. Independent of the rewrite finding; does not change any frozen or sealed record.

Also recommended: a research-log entry. D-172 (research-log.md:10878-10914) states the premise this overturns, "C4 could differ because it generates governed semantic queries", and the ei0.11.6 measurement has no ledger entry at all.

comments.author: sjarmak
comments.text:
C4 query-path disclosure executed (disclosure half of the decision to disclose and reinterpret, and to run E02 as the named contrast).

Finding disclosed: Omni's own agent chose the raw-SQL rewrite path on every C4 attempt. All 135 governed semantic queries carry rewriteSql true and aiGenerated true; join_via_map is empty on all 135. The harness posts only modelId, progressWebhookEnabled, prompt and branchId; the prompt is the bare question; rewriteSql, userEditedSQL, join_via_map and aiGenerated appear nowhere under src/, and no mode flag exists. The conservative HKB compilation deferred 511 of 1090 definitions (46.9%) as cross-grain, so deployed topics emit empty joins and no measures; for the 62 of 133 parseable multi-source attempts rewrite was the only available path. The planner then could not type output columns of SQL it did not compose, which is the shape of the 31 UNKNOWN-type terminal failures. The model was used as a vocabulary, not a compiler: 109 of 135 attempts reference a compiled dimension on the input side, but of 518 selected field references only 75 are compiled and 0 attempts select exclusively compiled fields.

Cost stated plainly in every edited document: the study can no longer claim it isolated semantic-layer query composition. C4 versus C3 no longer differs on who composes the query or on join and aggregation semantics. It still differs on the agent, on field resolution at rewrite time, on the execution contract, and on the accessible surface. Model parity would not restore the composition contrast.

title: Retain SQLSTATE in direct-capture telemetry so failure origin is derivable
description:
postgres_execution._execution_error computes the SQLSTATE and uses it to pick a
kind (timeout / infrastructure / statement), then direct_sql_capture.py keeps
only error.kind:

    except PostgreSQLExecutionError as error:
        self._record_database_queries(max(1, error.statement_index + 1))
        execution = database_failure(f"database_{error.kind}_error")

The SQLSTATE is discarded and appears in no artifact. Consequence: every non-08
SQLSTATE collapses into database_statement_error, so the artifacts cannot
separate 42P01 undefined_table from 42703 undefined_column from a genuine model
SQL defect. That is the difference between a broken benchmark environment and an
incorrect system outcome, and failure_origin is computed from failure_class
alone (direct_capture_telemetry.failure_origin).

This is why the organ_transplant_large / mental_healths_large classification
(omni-benchmark-2j9) had to be reconstructed by joining action-evidence SQL text
to per-seq trace status. That reconstruction works but it is not the contract
doing its job.

CORRECTION 2026-08-31 (audit omni-benchmark-gve.3). The original text called this
"purely additive telemetry". The semantics are additive; the cost is not. Every
carrier on the path is exact-set validated against a pinned schema version, so
there is no additive field anywhere:

  - direct_trace_validation._validate_trace_event rejects an event unless
    set(event) == TRACE_EVENT_FIELDS and schema_version == "trace-event-v2".
  - direct_capture_receipt.validate_capture_receipt_payload rejects a receipt
    unless set(value) == _FIELDS and schema_version == 4, and the capture
    summary is exact-set validated against _SUMMARY_FIELDS.
  - autoresearch_artifacts._validate_trace_record rejects a run record whose
    trace_schema_version is not TRACE_SCHEMA_VERSION.

So retaining SQLSTATE means a coordinated bump: trace-event-v2 to v3, capture
receipt 4 to 5, plus _SUMMARY_FIELDS. Under the pin-per-series drift rule
proposed in docs/protocol-amendment-dev-tier-draft.md, that is a new series with
a bridge round, not a fix landed against the frozen sealed-final-v6 series whose
artifacts are trace-event-v2 and receipt 4.

A second constraint: DirectExecution.payload is the tool payload the model sees.
SQLSTATE must not go there. The carrier has to be a telemetry-only channel
(a new DirectExecution.diagnostics field, or a parameter on database_failure that
never reaches payload), or the fix changes the evaluated system's inputs.

Landed toward this in the audit pass: the version literal now has one definition
site. omni_attempt._trace_fields and direct_sql_attempt._trace_fields each wrote
"trace-event-v2" as a literal while the validator compared against the
TRACE_SCHEMA_VERSION constant; both now import the constant, the validator's
error message interpolates it, and tests/test_trace_schema_version_binding.py
fails if any runtime module spells a version out for itself. The v3 bump is now
a one-line edit plus the deliberate tripwire assertion in that test file.

Remaining work is the schema bump itself and belongs to the round-2 series
opener, not to this frozen series.

title: Automate immutable Claude OAuth lease preflight
description: The direct benchmark needs automated, immutable Claude OAuth lease preparation without live credential refresh. Measurements show a 0700 isolated profile containing a valid access token and minimal non-secret configuration survives pinning and a completed read-only invocation byte-for-byte; cloning is not itself the failure when token headroom exceeds the run and every source identity is quiescent. Build a preflight that selects dedicated identities, verifies no attached sessions, requires access-token headroom greater than maximum run duration plus margin, constructs a 0700 minimal lease, verifies the pinned binary version/SHA, and forbids every writer/refresh process until release.
design: For benchmark runs, refresh-before-freeze and then hold still. Never refresh or copy back underneath verify_unchanged. The general fleet may keep a broker/keepalive, but it must surrender an identity for the entire benchmark lease. Preflight checks: source session count zero; source/lease 0700; credentials 0600; exact minimal config; access-token expiry beyond the scheduled wall bound and margin; refresh token never exercised during lease; exact committed Claude binary version/SHA. Lease artifacts expose only opaque hashes/expiry, never token content. Existing interrupted baseline remains frozen at its committed system configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic/live-public tests prove 0700 lease creation, minimal config, access-token headroom refusal, attached-session refusal, committed binary version/SHA match, three sequential immutable invocations without source/lease mutation, and fail-closed behavior on any mutation. No mid-run refresh, token copy-back, or competing session. Account-specific lease creation remains outside git and secrets never enter output. Integration is used only when compatible with the frozen baseline or in a separately frozen run.
notes:
Measured launch issue after lease handoff: exact frozen source at 5be315e was rejected because the parent process wrote pycs that child processes recompiled under different Python hash seeds; modules containing unordered constants produced different byte sequences. This is a pre-invocation infrastructure failure. For immediate immutable canary, remove ignored pycs and launch parent+children with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. Durable preflight should avoid treating byte-for-byte pyc equality as a source-integrity oracle.
2026-08-28T19:30Z: exact 2.1.250 frozen-transport canary public-baseline-v1-lease-canary-v2-20260828-1525 completed 12/12 at concurrency 3: 11 answered, 1 no_answer_insufficient_context, zero infrastructure failures/retries, 2,161,895 tokens, 5.5811165 measured notional cost. The immediate pyc workaround was PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 from parent launch after moving ignored pycs out of the worktree. Durable preflight change remains separate.
Partial delivery (uncommitted, main worktree). src/omni_benchmark/claude_lease_preflight.py + tests/test_claude_lease_preflight.py (19 tests) implement three of the design's checks: at least one slot; every slot's access-token headroom strictly greater than the attempt bound; and an optional --identity-stable-until wall that refuses to launch when a scheduled rotation lands inside the attempt window. Wired into baseline_batch_cli._execute_live immediately before run_baseline_batch. Error messages carry a sha256 slot identity, never a path or token.

Still unimplemented from the design: source session count zero, source/lease 0700 and credentials 0600 assertions, exact-minimal-config assertion, pinned binary version/SHA check. Slot-to-source correspondence is deliberately excluded from the harness module (a deployment fact, not a property of the evaluated system) and belongs to the lease-building operator tooling.

Measured correction to the design's premise: claude-refresh-all iterates /home/ds/.claude-homes/account{1..5} only and has no reference to /home/ds/.claude-leases, so a cron pass cannot mutate a lease directory or trip verify_unchanged(). The binding constraint on a run is the lease access-token expiry (currently 2026-08-29T02:54Z), not the 6h cron boundary. Whether a source-home refresh invalidates the lease's access token is still unobserved; the 23:00Z pass is the first test.
Coverage gap found and closed. The preflight was wired only into baseline_batch_cli._execute_live, but baseline_continuation_cli._execute constructs LiveBaselineDispatcher and calls run_baseline_batch directly without passing through it. The live 518-attempt continuation dispatches through the continuation path, so the gate would not have fired on the launch that will actually hit its credential wall. Now gated at the top of _execute, before the dispatcher and the database environment directory are constructed, so a refusal costs nothing; --identity-stable-until added to the continuation parser for parity. Test test_execute_refuses_when_a_lease_expires_inside_the_attempt_bound asserts run_baseline_batch is never reached. Suite 1443 passed / 3 skipped, ruff clean. Uncommitted in main.

General lesson worth carrying: this codebase has two live-dispatch entrypoints, and a preflight is only as good as the narrowest one it covers. Any future launch gate needs wiring into both.
Comparator OAuth pool is now four slots. Leased /home/ds/.claude-leases/omni-a5 from account5 (fingerprint 7eb167203f8d, matches source); .lease-rebuild.sh and the lane monitor cover slots 1, 3, 4, 5. account2 is permanently retired: never leased, never counted as capacity, and its logged-out state is expected. Its removal from /home/ds/.gc/account-identity.map is a fleet action outside this repo; until then claude-refresh-all alerts on it every 6h.

Dispatch timeout default lowered 1800s -> 900s in both live entrypoints. Slowest attempt observed on the 16db continuation was 156s, so 900s keeps a wide margin for slower databases while capping what one wedged attempt holds a slot for, and it halves the token headroom verify_lease_window demands since the attempt bound is what it compares tokens against. Future launches only. Test: test_dispatch_timeout_default_bounds_a_stuck_attempt_without_failing_slow_ones. Suite 1444 passed / 3 skipped, ruff clean, all still uncommitted in main.
2026-08-29 main-only consolidation: the tracked uncommitted lease-preflight integration was deliberately excluded from canonical main because credential/OAuth/lease work is out of scope. Its complete tracked patch is preserved in stash main-pre-consolidation-tracked-20260829T1748-0400 (full stash patch SHA-256 1320b69b9335b330c14e245bccfdee1da761453b54da62c03d81ea87b578ef80); untracked src/omni_benchmark/claude_lease_preflight.py and tests/test_claude_lease_preflight.py remain untouched in the main worktree. Resume only in an isolated worktree under operator-owned lease authority; do not apply the whole stash to main.

title: Specify LiveSQLBench Large-v1 evaluation and pre-gold protocol
description: Design a rigorous, publishable Omni evaluation of non-CRUD LiveSQLBench Large-v1. Research only public materials, resolve experimental decisions collaboratively, create a deterministic leakage-resistant train/test protocol, and establish the durable project goal before any gold-answer access.
design: Primary estimand: Given an existing semantic model for a database, how accurately does Omni answer previously unseen analytical questions, and do semantic-layer/harness improvements developed on other questions generalize to those unseen questions? Use deterministic 231 train / 101 test question-level split across all 18 DBs, with database as primary stratification and public metadata balanced where feasible. Full public schema and HKB for every DB are available during model construction; held-out question ground truth and hidden annotations are inaccessible until freeze. Database-specific model changes based only on that DB's training questions are allowed. Secondary: 18-fold leave-one-database-out transformation portability within the 231-question development partition. Tertiary: preregistered raw-schema / HKB-context / Omni-semantic ablation if fair and technically feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Public benchmark structure and knowledge-base semantics are documented; eligible non-CRUD manifest and deterministic representative split design are specified; gold-access guard is enforced; user and agent reach shared understanding on material experimental forks; resulting goal is recorded.
notes:
Custody decision: hard human-custody seal. Before private data: commit eligible manifest, deterministic 231/101 split and IDs, extraction/evaluation boundary, and EVALUATION_PROTOCOL.md; precommit only format-independent tooling if attachment schema is not sufficiently documented. User keeps untouched attachment outside agent-accessible workspace and records SHA-256 without content inspection. A deterministic train-only extraction releases 231 private records to ignored private/train; hidden test fields never enter development. Freeze all semantic models/harness/config/prompts/versions and commit a machine-readable freeze manifest. A dedicated sealed evaluator receives the untouched source, selects only precommitted 101 IDs, executes comparison, and emits scores/permitted aggregates without gold SQL. Record source SHA-256, split commit, final commit, run timestamp/config, artifacts. Public text/metadata for all 332 may stay committed. Hidden external_knowledge/test cases for train may be available but their permitted experimental role is still to be resolved.
Public reconnaissance (official releases only; no gold accessed): HF commit a418e108d5cbb4cf9b783a928eff5e924ad2460d; official harness commit e15cd221267e06fabfaf6a3d4a69308280ce9a7c. Public JSONL has 480 rows: 332 Query and 148 Management. Query tasks span all 18 DBs (10-24 each), 181 high_level=true / 151 false; no public difficulty_tier; private sol_sql/external_knowledge/test_cases arrays empty. Across HKBs: 1,090 definitions (430 calculation, 462 domain, 198 value illustration), 560 dependent definitions and 945 declared edges. Official SELECT evaluator removes DISTINCT from both SQLs, executes with 60s timeout, normalizes dates/JSON/numerics (default 2 decimals), then compares ordered lists when conditions.order=true and sets otherwise. gas-city reuse: provenance ledger, pinned build, isolated fixtures, mutation-proven assertions, browser-authored Omni models/topics and three-leg outside-SQL/Omni-SQL/Omni-topic parity.
Held-out matrix decision: freeze and score all four conditions together on the 101 test questions. C1 Raw SQL = schema/raw representation/no enforcement. C2 HKB-reference SQL = schema+HKB/raw HKB available via reasonable programmatic/search access/optional use. C3 Omni-model SQL = schema+HKB/exported Omni semantic model available via equivalent reference access/optional use. C4 Governed Omni = schema+HKB/Omni semantic model/enforced semantic compilation and production validation. Primary endpoint is frozen C4 execution accuracy. Prespecified confirmatory paired contrasts: C2-C1 business knowledge; C3-C2 structured semantic representation; C4-C3 enforcement/governance/harness; C4-C1 total system effect. Freeze and reasonably develop all four on train. Match exogenous resources (base model/version where possible, question, DB, execution, time/token/tool/retry budgets, source knowledge, scorer); preserve intrinsic architecture. Document unavoidable model/tool asymmetry. Report paired deltas with CIs and McNemar tests; do not promote whichever contrast looks best. No full-context dump requirement for C2/C3; provide fair search/retrieval access.
Repeat/statistics decision: 3 sealed repetitions per condition = 1,212 frozen outputs. Sole primary endpoint: C4 run-1 accuracy on 101. Run-1 C1-C4 paired confirmatory contrasts; mechanistic C2-C1/C3-C2/C4-C3 use Holm correction for significance tests; C4-C1 overall contrast. Three-run analyses: per-run accuracy; per-question 3/3,2/3,1/3,0/3 correctness; correctness flips; no-answer/system failure; result-set agreement; latency/cost; question-clustered bootstrap CIs. Separate outcome reliability from result reliability; SQL variability diagnostic only. No voting/selection. Commit deterministic block-interleaved order over question x condition x repetition with repetitions separated; record timestamps/model IDs. All 1,212 generations complete before any gold scoring or result release. Normal evaluated-system retries are frozen; exhaustion counts incorrect/no-answer. Exogenous evaluator/DB/network failures may be rerun only under prespecified, logged criteria using the same trial identity; agent/harness failures are not infrastructure failures.
Information-tier decision: (1) public schema/HKB/questions available in development and runtime, frozen for test; (2) hidden train SQL/test cases/external_knowledge available only as offline supervision after pre-supervision baseline, never question-specific runtime inputs; (3) hidden test fields sealed-evaluator only. Preserve public-only mechanical HKB-to-Omni baseline before releasing train labels. Treat external_knowledge as privileged diagnostic oracle metadata: measure whether required nodes exist, dependencies compile, retrieval can reach them, and recurring classes fail; never use IDs to select runtime context. Gold-driven changes must be reusable system/model rules, not question-ID exceptions. Sample queries must encode reusable patterns, contain no benchmark question-to-gold pairs or IDs at runtime, have experiment/rationale/provenance/count, and receive an ablation if materially impactful. Final claim must acknowledge supervised development on 231 questions, not zero-shot.
Model-parity decision: C4 uses production-default Omni, unchanged except in-scope semantic-model/harness improvements. Inspect/record provider, observable model identifiers, tier(s), reasoning/token settings, retries, and stage-specific model use. Match C1-C3 exactly to C4 when independently invocable; otherwise pin one capable model across C1-C3. Production fidelity outranks forcing C4 parity. Predeclare interpretation before scoring: if exact parity, C4-C3 is an approximate controlled architectural contrast subject to remaining differences; if not, it is only a production-system comparison. C2-C1 and C3-C2 remain controlled within the matched direct-SQL system.

title: Populate cost_usd from AI credit-usage deltas instead of recording it unavailable
description:
The harness records cost_usd = None, cost_source = "unavailable",
cost_unavailable_reason = "omni_job_api_does_not_expose_cost" for every governed
attempt (sealed_omni_adapter.py:105, baseline_attempt_adapter.py:389). Verified
2026-08-31 against the live CLI: that reason is still accurate for the job API.
ai job-status and ai job-result carry no cost field, and ai conversations-list
returns only id, name, createdAt, updatedAt, and a prompt summary.

Credits ARE readable, per user and cumulative:

  POST /api/v1/ai/credit-usage/users   (omni ai credit-usage-users-read)
  body {"userIds": ["<membershipId from omni whoami>"]}
  -> {"periodStart", "periodEnd", "users": [{"userId", "creditsUsed"}]}

1 credit = 1 USD. The period is the calendar month in UTC and the counter resets
at the boundary. August 2026 for the benchmark identity read 635.297481375,
captured at experiments/analysis/omni-credit-usage-2026-08.json.

Proposal: bracket each attempt with a credit read before and after, and record
the delta as cost_usd with cost_source = "credit_usage_delta". The counter
carries nine decimal places, so a single attempt resolves exactly; the two reads
are metadata calls and consume no credits themselves.

Preconditions that make the number meaningful, all of which need enforcing in
code rather than assumed:

1. Sole consumer. Any other use of that identity inside the bracket lands in the
   same counter. The account demonstrably has non-benchmark AI traffic, so this
   is a live risk, not a theoretical one. Enforce by failing the attempt if the
   run does not hold an exclusive lease on the identity.
2. Serialization. Attempts running concurrently under one identity cannot be
   attributed individually. Either run the arm serially or record cost at batch
   granularity with an explicit aggregate marker.
3. Period boundary. A bracket spanning the month rollover sees the counter reset
   and computes a negative delta. Reject any bracket whose two reads report
   different periodStart values rather than recording a wrong number.
4. Read failure. A failed post-read must not silently produce cost_usd = None
   that looks like the existing "unavailable" case. Give it a distinct
   cost_source so the two are separable in analysis.

Out of scope: retroactive cost for C1-C4. The counter is cumulative, those
attempts are past, and the no-rerun rule forbids re-running to collect cost.
Their cost column stays unavailable, with the mechanism and its limits
documented.

Value: turns cost-per-correct-answer into a reportable metric alongside
accuracy, which is a stronger claim about the semantic layer than accuracy on
its own. Governed and direct arms differ in context size, so a per-arm cost
number is a real result rather than bookkeeping.

Acceptance: a governed arm runs with cost_usd populated from a bracketed delta,
all four preconditions enforced with tests, and the resulting per-arm cost
appears in the analysis output.
notes:
PLAN: Bracket each governed Omni attempt with a credit-usage read and record the delta as cost_usd.

Goal: a C4 attempt records a measured cost_usd from a before/after credit read, with all
four preconditions enforced in code, and a separable non-null reason when it cannot.

Verified facts (2026-08-31, live CLI, read-only):
- omni ai credit-usage-users-read takes body {"userIds": [uuid]} -> {periodStart, periodEnd,
  users:[{userId, creditsUsed}]}; --schema confirms the shape. No per-job resolution.
- omni whoami whoami returns user.membershipId = 595a871e-e5a9-46b7-a208-f8920da67263, the
  exact id the evidence file used. The user id is therefore derivable from the whoami the
  probe already performs; no new identity env var is required.
- autoresearch_capture_policy._validate_sources restricts cost_source to
  provider_reported | derived | unavailable and enforces cost_usd null iff unavailable.
  A new source value is unavoidable and must be added there.

Approach:
1. New module omni_credit_cost.py: whoami -> membership id; CreditUsageReading with strict
   response validation; AttemptCost; resolve_attempt_cost(before, after) returning
   credit_usage_delta on success, or unavailable with reason credit_usage_period_rollover
   (differing periodStart), credit_usage_nonmonotonic (negative delta), or
   credit_usage_read_failed (post-read raised); non-blocking fcntl.flock lease on a file
   keyed by base-url origin plus user id.
2. omni_cli.OmniCliClient.credit_usage(user_ids) over ai credit-usage-users-read with JSON
   stdin, bounded and uuid-validated, using the idempotent observer retry path.
3. Opt-in via OMNI_COST_BRACKET_LEASE_DIR. Unset reproduces today's record byte for byte.
   Set means lease plus pre-read happen before job submission; either failing refuses the
   launch instead of writing a corrupted attempt.
4. C4AttemptSpec gains cost: AttemptCost | None; omni_attempt._telemetry_fields emits from
   it, defaulting to the current unavailable triple.
5. autoresearch_capture_policy: widen cost_source with credit_usage_delta only.
6. Wire the three C4 capture sites: omni_probe_cli._run_attempt,
   baseline_attempt_adapter._capture_public_baseline_omni, sealed_omni_factory probe runner.
7. Docs: harness-disclosure telemetry contract and its residual limits, research-log entry.

Files: new src/omni_benchmark/omni_credit_cost.py and tests/test_omni_credit_cost.py; edit
omni_cli.py, omni_attempt.py, autoresearch_capture_policy.py, omni_probe_cli.py,
baseline_attempt_adapter.py, sealed_omni_factory.py, tests/test_omni_cli.py,
docs/harness-disclosure.md, docs/research-log.md.

Tests: resolution table over the four outcomes; malformed credit response rejection; lease
exclusivity within one process; CLI argv and stdin shape; telemetry emission with and
without bracketing; regression pinning the disabled path to the record shape shipped today.

Risks:
- cost_source is a validated surface frozen artifacts pass through. The change only widens
  the accepted set, so every existing record stays valid; a test pins that.
- The lease enforces harness-side exclusivity only. A browser session on the same identity
  is undetectable and would inflate a delta. Documented as a residual limit.
- Batch dispatch can schedule C4 concurrently. With bracketing on, the second attempt
  refuses to launch. Deliberate, but a bracketed arm has to be scheduled serially.

Deviations from the bead text, for approval:
- Precondition 4 asks for a distinct cost_source per failure. Success gets its own
  cost_source; failures separate through the existing cost_unavailable_reason field, which
  exists for exactly this and keeps cost_source a small closed vocabulary.
- Precondition 1 says fail the attempt. The failure lands at launch, before job submission,
  so a cost-instrumentation problem never manufactures an evaluated-system or
  infrastructure failure record or collides with the no-rerun rule.

Out of scope: retroactive cost for C1-C4; scheduler changes to force serialization; per-job
attribution, which the API does not offer; non-C4 conditions, which already report cost.

RESULT: Bracketed credit-usage cost is implemented, tested, and documented. One
acceptance clause remains open and needs a live governed pass.

New: src/omni_benchmark/omni_credit_cost.py, tests/test_omni_credit_cost.py (54 tests).

Mechanism. capture_with_cost(client, environment, capture) takes the capture as a
callable so the post-read cannot be mis-ordered by a caller. Order is whoami ->
membership id -> exclusive lease -> pre-read -> capture -> post-read -> the probe
with cost attached. Opt-in through OMNI_COST_BRACKET_LEASE_DIR; unset reproduces
today's record field for field, pinned by a regression test.

The four preconditions, each enforced in code:
1. Sole consumer: non-blocking fcntl.flock on a 0600 file named by sha256 of the
   membership id. A second harness attempt on that identity refuses to launch.
2. Serialization: same lease, taken before the pre-read, so a nested bracket
   never even reads the counter.
3. Period boundary: both reads carry their period bounds; a mismatch records
   credit_usage_period_rollover, a backwards move records credit_usage_nonmonotonic.
4. Read failure: a failed pre-read refuses the launch before any spend; a failed
   post-read keeps the attempt and records credit_usage_read_failed, distinct from
   omni_job_api_does_not_expose_cost.

Surfaces changed:
- OmniCliClient.credit_usage(user_ids) over ai credit-usage-users-read with JSON
  stdin, uuid-validated and unique, on the idempotent observer retry path.
  _run_observer_json now forwards stdin.
- OmniProbeResult gains cost: AttemptCost | None. Cost is an observation, next to
  tokens and latency, not pre-attempt configuration.
- omni_attempt._telemetry_fields emits from probe.cost, defaulting to the
  unavailable triple.
- autoresearch_capture_policy: cost_source gains exactly one value,
  credit_usage_delta. token_source keeps its original three, so a token count
  cannot claim to be a credit measurement. Widening only, so frozen records stay valid.
- Three C4 capture sites wired: omni_probe_cli._execute_probe,
  baseline_attempt_adapter._capture_public_baseline_omni, sealed_omni_factory._run_probe.

Two integration points the change had to fix, not just add to:
- baseline_batch._hard_budget_cost demanded exactly the job-API reason for a null
  C4 cost. A rollover or failed read would have failed the batch's cost accounting.
  It now accepts the four named reasons and still rejects an unexplained null.
  With a measured cost, BatchTelemetry.total_cost_usd stops being null for a
  governed batch: that is where the per-arm number surfaces, no new analysis code.
- SEALED_RUNTIME_SOURCE_PATHS had to list omni_credit_cost.py, or
  verify_sealed_runtime_sources would not bind the new runtime source to the frozen
  commit. test_runtime_source_set_is_closed_over_static_local_imports caught it.

Docs: harness-disclosure telemetry contract vocabulary plus a 2026-08-31 cost
addendum; research-log D-210.

Gates: ruff check and format clean; full suite 2263 passed, 3 skipped; project
coverage 84.01% against fail_under=80; omni_credit_cost.py at 97% branch coverage.

OPEN, needs a live pass: acceptance asks that a governed arm actually run with
cost_usd populated. That is an evaluated live action against a metered identity,
so it is not taken here. What it needs: an identity that is otherwise idle, an
absolute existing lease directory in OMNI_COST_BRACKET_LEASE_DIR, and serial C4
scheduling (baseline_batch_live has a c4_concurrency_canary_schedule; with
bracketing on, a concurrent second attempt refuses to launch by design).

Limits disclosed rather than closed: the lease binds harness processes only, so a
browser session spending on the same identity inside a bracket would inflate the
delta; and the endpoint reports whole-account credits, so the delta measures what
the account spent during the attempt, not a figure the provider attributes to it.

Out of scope as the bead states: no retroactive cost for C1-C4.
close_reason: Implementation, tests, and documentation complete; full suite 2267 passed, 3 skipped, coverage 83.62% against fail_under=80, ruff clean. The remaining acceptance clause, a live governed arm running with cost_usd populated from a bracketed delta, is an evaluated live action against a metered identity and moved to omni-benchmark-r5a with its preconditions. Nothing committed: the working tree already carried uncommitted D-209 semantic-field-kinds work before this task.

title: Guard _exact_binomial_two_sided against negative counts on the next analysis unfreeze

title: Quality CI test step needs ~40 minutes; make it faster instead of raising the cap
description:
The Quality workflow's test step needs about 40 minutes on a GitHub 4-vCPU runner and has been growing. Raising timeout-minutes is a stopgap, not a fix; this bead is for the fix.

Measured, not estimated. In run 33420484237 the job spent 7 seconds on checkout, uv install, Python install, and dependency sync combined, then 30 minutes 5 seconds in "Run tests with branch coverage" before the 30-minute cap killed it at 76% of the suite (last line: tests/test_sealed_batch.py). Extrapolating uniformly puts the step near 40 minutes. Runs on 2026-08-30T23:17 and 2026-08-31T01:41 finished in 25m13s and 25m28s total, so the step grew roughly 60% in about a day, which tracks the C5 test additions.

Directions worth measuring, cheapest first:

1. pytest-xdist with -n auto. The runner has 4 vCPUs and the suite is single-threaded, so this is the largest available win. pytest-cov combines per-worker coverage data, so the fail_under=80 branch gate survives. Risk is test isolation: 110 subprocess call sites and 96 git invocations across 157 test files, and any test assuming a shared cwd, a shared tmp directory, or serial ordering will surface here. Validate with a full local -n auto run before committing.

2. Find out what is actually slow. Run pytest --durations=50 and check whether the time concentrates in a few files (test_sealed_dispatch, test_custody, test_dev_a_baseline_scoring, and test_omni_probe_cli each carry 9 or 10 subprocess call sites) or is spread evenly at roughly 300 ms per test.

3. Measure the coverage tracer's share. branch=true costs real time; if it is a large fraction, one option is to run the gate on a schedule and keep per-push runs uninstrumented.

Do not treat a raised timeout as the resolution. Close this only when the step is measurably faster.
close_reason:
Done in 276d9c3, direction 1 plus the direction-2 measurement that justified it.

Profile (pytest --durations under coverage, local): seven synthetic custody
tests are 72% of the suite. 258s test_score_freezes_gold_then_returns_complete_sql_free_results,
219s test_matched_frame_scores_and_publishes_all_1068_attempts,
205s test_c5_single_database_load_reproduces_the_full_candidates_plan,
193s test_live_c5_deployment_carries_only_the_scheduled_committed_plans,
182s test_dry_c5_plan_is_exact_public_and_provider_inert,
180s test_live_c5_deployment_requires_a_profile_before_product_access,
133s test_real_production_factories_complete_all_1212_synthetic_attempts.
All CPU-bound loops over the 1068- and 1212-attempt frames. Coverage tracing
is most of the cost: 663s without --cov, 1900s with it.

The isolation risk the bead flagged did not materialize. The only
session-scoped fixture builds its stub Claude binary through tmp_path_factory,
which is per-worker; the one monkeypatch.chdir is function-scoped; the
Path("runs/...") occurrences are configuration values, not writes.

pytest-xdist -n 4 with coverage: 1900s -> 778s, 2.4x, 2117 passed / 3 skipped,
combined branch coverage 83.51%, so fail_under=80 holds across worker data.
-n 4 rather than -n auto because a public repository gets 4 vCPUs from GitHub,
which is the configuration measured. timeout-minutes restored to 30.

Not done, and not needed yet: making the seven tests themselves cheaper. If
the suite grows back into the cap, that is the next lever, and it is real work
on custody-protocol tests rather than a config change.

title: Separate durable harness from one-shot episode code for the public artifact
description:
The durable, reusable tunable harness is roughly 22-24K lines out of 52.6K total src lines. The remainder includes about 6K lines of single-episode gate artifacts that exist to execute one specific evaluation episode rather than to be reused: c4_result_recovery (756 lines), baseline_continuation (944 lines) plus its CLI (342 lines), sealed_mvp_frame (175 lines), dev_a_gold_conformance (593 lines), gold_free_scoring (407 lines), c1_retrieval_sensitivity (523 lines), dump_coverage (132 lines), and e02 CLI machinery. For the public research artifact, this episode-specific code should move into a clearly labeled area (for example an experiments/episodes or similar directory) so a reader can tell the durable, reusable harness apart from one-off gate execution scripts. This directly serves the goal of making the repository approachable as a public artifact: someone browsing src/ should see the harness, not a pile of single-use CLIs.

For external communication about this repository, the recommended pitch order is findings first (the C2-vs-C4 gap, the 34 contract failures, the grain-contract analysis) and the harness second, since the findings are what make the work interesting and the harness is supporting infrastructure. This bead shares the same timing constraint as the consolidation bead: do not start until the optimized candidate is frozen, since Freeze-B diffs against the frozen baseline commit and file-moves would pollute that comparison.

title: Consolidate duplicated harness machinery after optimized-arm freeze
description:
Two attempt-repository implementations have diverged by copy-adaptation rather than shared abstraction: ImmutableAttemptRepository in baseline_batch.py (1451 lines) and SealedAttemptRepository in sealed_generation_staging.py (666 lines). Five preflight modules independently implement overlapping checks: omni_probe_preflight, direct_capture_binding, direct_attempt_binding, claude_lease_preflight, and preflight_sealed_dispatch in sealed_dispatch.py; these should sit behind one interface. Canonicalization primitives are separately reimplemented across the codebase: _canonical_json appears 14 times, _sha256 11 times, _identifier 10 times, _digest 9 times; these belong in one shared module next to content_policy.py. There are also 26 separate argparse parser implementations that should collapse into shared parser construction. Consolidating this machinery is estimated to remove 4-6K lines with no change to evaluation semantics, since it is pure internal deduplication of already-frozen behavior.

HARD CONSTRAINT: this work must not start before the optimized candidate is frozen. Freeze-B reviews diff the frozen candidate against the frozen baseline commit, and refactor churn touching these modules during that window would pollute those diffs and make the reviewed change harder to verify.
close_reason: Deliberately deferred beyond the MVP: reviewer feedback and the stop-after-E02 rule favor a simple reviewer surface over a risky post-result 4-6K-line refactor. Existing behavior stays frozen.

title: Report must state the token reduction as a bounded-payload claim, not a system-cost claim
description:
Tracking a framing commitment, so it is not lost between now and the write-up.

An external stakeholder has the figure "~100x fewer tokens via progressive
discovery / intelligent schema retrieval" from a progress email. As written that
is defensible and describes the retrieval payload. It is not defensible as a
statement about system cost.

What the evidence supports:
  inspect_schema returned the entire schema (51 tables, ~170K input tokens in the
  following turn) at commit 349e0bb. Since 2b72244 it returns at most 4 tables and
  64 KiB, enforced structurally. Two orders of magnitude, guaranteed by the bound
  rather than measured.

What it does NOT support:
  The 1,585-token / $0.017715 replay figure is an aborted attempt. It terminated
  at forbidden_tool_payload before any database query, and the research log
  records "end-to-end success remains unproven". It is 170K-before-failing versus
  1.6K-before-failing; neither run answered.

Ground truth from public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1 (518 captures):
  median input tokens  c1 127,310  c2 198,968  c3 152,976
  mean cost            c1 $1.48    c2 $1.71    c3 $1.84
  turns per attempt    median 5, max 12
  largest single turn  median 61,892, p99 184,543
  attempts with any turn >=169,995: 12 of 518 (2.3%)
  model_budget_error: 17 of 518 (3.3%), down from deterministic on the canary

Requirement: the write-up states the bounded-payload claim with its bound, and
gives per-attempt cost separately, so the two cannot be conflated. Lead with the
precise version rather than presenting it as a retraction.
close_reason: Current results report cleanly separates the structural payload bound from system cost and preserves the aborted-diagnostic caveat.
